## §281 — `List.reduce()` into a method returning `String` compiled clean and died at LOAD with `VerifyError: Bad return type` (no `checkcast` before `areturn`) — ✅ FIXED 18/09 (lane compiler `.22`, #394)

**Symptom (measured pre-fix, tip jar):** the #394 verbatim (`build(): String { return parts.reduce("", (acc: String, s: String) -> { return acc + s }) }`) built with zero diagnostics and crashed at class load: the erased `kof_list_reduce` returns `Object` and the value was returned straight into a `String`-declared `areturn`.

**Root cause:** `JvmOpCollections.emitKofRuntimeCall` post-call handling had two reduce paths — the generic reference branch excluded `String` (it is special-cased elsewhere) and the primitive branch only matched numeric returns — a reference (String) result fell through the gap and got **no cast at all**.

**Fix (root cause, additive):** the shared reduce branch now emits `CHECKCAST` for any `ClassType` (reference) result when the static-call return is declared `Object` — the same treatment classes already got; primitive unboxing is untouched (the `6`/`11` controls prove it).

**Proof:** `ReduceStringCastTest` 4/4 — verbatim EXECUTES `hello world` (Q0: stashing the fix turns the two run-asserts RED — the VerifyError is a LOAD failure, so only execution proves it), faces cover reference-as-var (`.length` = 11), the pre-existing primitive path (Int sum = 6) and a class-reduce compile control; CLI measured `hello world/11/6` on **all four targets** (rule 5 — the gap was JVM-only, the goldens now agree cross-target).

## §282 — lambda using an instance field of the enclosing class compiled clean and died at LOAD with `VerifyError: Bad type on operand stack` (the emitter pushed the Lambda object where the value belonged) — ✅ FIXED 18/09 (lane compiler `.22`, #381)

**Symptom (measured pre-fix, tip jar):** the #381 verbatim (`getMultiplier(): (Int) -> Int { return (x: Int) -> { return x * factor } }`) produced `Lambda0.invoke(int) = iload_1, **aload_0**, imul, ireturn` — `factor` resolved to slot 0 of the synthetic class, i.e. the Lambda's own `this` (no fields, no captures). The script interpreter showed the same root through the shared IR: `println(multiply(5))` → `not an int: Lambda0@…`.

**Root cause:** the capture collector (`CompilerCaptures.collectCapturesExpr`) only matched names against **outer locals** — an enclosing instance field is not a local, stayed a free name, and the identifier emitter's LAST fallback (`ExpressionLowerer` :121) silently pushed `aload_0` (an R6-shaped silent miscompile: wrong type on the stack, zero diagnostics).

**Fix (root cause, additive — captured by VALUE at the creation site):** the collector now resolves a free name against `currentLoweringOwner`'s hierarchy; a non-static field becomes a synthetic capture with sentinel index `< 0`. All six creation-site push loops (ExpressionLowerer, StatementLowerer×2, ExpressionStaticCallLowerer, CompilerUiEmitter) now go through `CompilerCaptures.pushCapture`, which for a sentinel emits `this.getfield` of the **enclosing** receiver — where `this` is the real object. Static fields keep the body's GETSTATIC path; an instance field in a static method is already blocked by SEM075 (§276), so the sentinel path only runs where a receiver exists. Backends share the IR: no per-target patch (MethodCtx re-homes captures by name, never by sentinel index).

**Proof:** `LambdaFieldCaptureTest` 4/4 — verbatim EXECUTES `15` (Q0: without the fix 3/4 RED on the run asserts), mixed field+mutated-local keeps the pre-existing by-reference local semantics (measured golden `102`, not the guessed `13` — r1), wide `Long` + `String` fields through the sentinel print `v=10000000005`; CLI measured `15` on **all four targets** (jvm/script/js/native). Coordination note: this repo is shared by several agents and `git stash` is per-repository — a lane popped a foreign `stash@{0}` mid-unit (entry kept, work preserved, lesson recorded): tag stashes (`stash push -m <lane>`) and never blind-pop.

## §285 — unannotated `listOf`/`setOf` with related subtypes inferred the element type from the FIRST argument (`checkcast Dog` on every get) → `ClassCastException` on any other element — ✅ FIXED 18/09 (lane compiler `.22`, #360)

**Symptom (measured pre-fix, tip jar):** `var animals = listOf(new Dog(), new Cat())` printed `woof` then `ClassCastException: class Cat cannot be cast to class Dog`; bytecode: `checkcast Dog` before both `invokevirtual sound`. The same first-wins ran through `setOf`.

**Root cause:** three copies of the collection element inference (`BuiltinCallTyper`, `CompilerTypeSupport.listOfElementType`, mirrored in the driver typer) kept `args[0]`'s type — the §156 lambda-heterogeneous face had already been fixed in this family by unification, the subtype face had not. The shared `commonSupertype` helper could not save it: it only walked the **superclass** chain, so `Dog`/`Cat` (common type = **interface** `Animal`) fell through to `Object`.

**Fix (additive, r1-safe):** uncollected related elements now widen to their named common ancestor (interface OR superclass) via a BFS closure in `HierarchyResolver` (`widenToCommonSupertype`), across all three inference copies. When the only common type is `Object`, the pre-fix first-wins stays (SEM056 already rejects truly heterogeneous literals — measured `A` + `"x"` → compile error); primitives and same-type lists are untouched by construction (equals → identity of the fold).

**Parity follow-up (docs lane, 18/09):** the proof's 4 cases cover JVM×3 + JS×1; the SCRIPT and NATIVE faces were then MEASURED by the docs lane on tip `d3598c2d` (fresh jars, 18/09): `kof script` → `woof/meow`, `run --target native` (x86-64 ELF) → `woof/meow` — 4-target agreement confirmed at the measured level. REMAINING: `conformance-matrix.md` still has no cell for subtype inference (only heterogeneous if/switch-expr rows, lines 66–69) — owner = the parity/compiler lane.
**Proof:** `HeterogeneousListInferTest` 4/4 — verbatim EXECUTES `woof\nmeow` (Q0: pre-fix checkout → 2/4 RED on the run asserts), faces: common **superclass** (A/B → `p/p`) + `setOf` contains `true`; controls: same-type list keeps the concrete type (`.a()` resolves only on A) and primitive arithmetic list unchanged (`2`); CLI measured `woof/meow` on **all four targets** (jvm/script/js/native). Numbering note: §279→§280→§285 — the same §176 collision pattern a third time in this session; take the tip number from the REMOTE before writing.

## §286 — `KofConcurrency2Test.cancelDoesNotLeakAcrossWorkersNative` goes RED under host load (sleep-based native timing test; family of §256 poll(b) load flake) — ✅ FIXED 18/09 (lane nat `192.168.100.17`) — not a timing margin: a REAL lost-cancel race in the spawn/cancel table

**Found/owner:** catalogued 18/09 ~04:3x UTC by lane `.22`; reproduced, root-caused and fixed by the nat lane (`.17`).

**Reproduction (measured).** Same ELF as the test, 40 runs under a 6-way concurrent native-build load: **1/40 miss**, mode `assertion failed` + **212 s** wall-clock (a `longo` that ran its full 100000 iterations — the cancel never landed). The original `.22` sighting (`VAZOU`, 126.9 s) is the SECOND mode of the same table — see (b).

**Root cause (a) — lost cancel in the start window.** `kof_spawn_handle_new` publishes state=2 and the TID (written by `pthread_create`) before the new thread runs; the cancel-table entry, however, is inserted only when the trampoline starts. A `cancel()` arriving in that window does `slot_find` → 0 → returns **false** (`assert(cancel)` dies) and the request is LOST — the worker, once scheduled, checks `cancelled()` and sees nothing. Under scheduler starvation (parallel builds) the window is wide (observed >15 ms).

**Root cause (b) — delete via recyclable handle (the `VAZOU`/999 mode).** The worker publishes `done=1` and THEN deletes its entry — reading the pointer via `handle->cancelEntry`. Between those two steps `await` can return and the handle memory be recycled by the next `spawn`; the late delete then clears the OTHER worker's slot (tid=0) while the owner's entry survives — possibly with flag=1 (a cancelled worker). Later TID reuse + a hole mid-cluster makes `insert` claim a SECOND slot for the same live TID (linear probing without backward-shift), and `cancelled()` finds the stale flagged entry first → a newborn worker reports cancelled (`999`/`VAZOU`); the mirrored form explains the full-run-slow sighting too.

**Fix (root, in the runtime — not test margins).** (i) the trampoline copies its entry pointer into its OWN FRAME (`40(%rsp)` x86 / `16(sp)` riscv) and the exit delete reads from there — handle recycling can no longer make a worker touch a foreign slot; (ii) `cancel()` with no entry marks **pending** in the handle (new slot: `48` x86 / `56` riscv; alloc 48→56 / 56→64), re-checks the entry after `mfence` / `fence rw,rw`, and returns true; the trampoline after inserting does the mirrored store→fence→load and applies the pending mark — classic Dekker, the window closes WITHOUT any scheduling assumption. Cooperative §117 semantics unchanged; additive for existing programs. aarch64 comes through `NativeAarch64Translator` (rule 5).

**Proof (same commit).** New deterministic window-hammer tests: `cancelImmediatelyAfterSpawnNative` (spawn+immediate cancel ×30 — old runtime **1/30**, new **30/30**) and `cancelImmediatelyAfterSpawnCrossArch` (riscv64+aarch64 ×10 under qemu — old **0/10**, new **10/10**); RED→GREEN measured by stashing only the runtime files. The §286 test itself: **0/60** misses under the same 6-way build-load hammer + **0/150** with 6 concurrent binaries (pre-fix: 1/40 + 212 s). NO assertion relaxed (Q5) — the "assumedTrue under load" suggested in the catalogue is NOT needed: the test was covering a real race and now passes for the right reason. `KofConcurrency2Test` **46/46**; neighbors `NativeRiscv64/Aarch64E2ETest` 45+45, `KofTimeE2ETest` 39/39, `KofObservabilityTest` 12/12, `SpawnE2ETest` 10, `SpawnAwaitBlockE2ETest` 5.

**Status.** ✅ FIXED 18/09. Related: §117 (the table), §291 (same family, different mechanism — closed today), §252/§256 (closed load-flake neighbors).
## §287 — fn-type inside a generic DECLARED type (`List<(Int) -> Int>`) rejected with SEM011 on parameter/field/return while the same local compiled — ✅ FIXED 18/09 (lane compiler `.22`, #374)

**Symptom (measured on tip):** `applyFirst(fns: List<(Int) -> Int>, ...)` → `:0:0: error: Undefined variable or type: 'List<(Int) -> Int>' in parameter 'fns' [SEM011]`; the SAME type as a local variable compiled and ran. `Map<Int, () -> Void>` as a parameter and `List<() -> Void>` as a field were the other two faces.

**Root cause:** `MemberResolver.declaredTypeUnresolved` (the §251 shared predicate) tested `contains(" -> ")` BEFORE the `<...>` generic branch. A nested arrow inside the type arguments was taken as the connective of the whole string: `List<(Int) -> Int>` was parsed as a "function" whose return is the garbage `Int>` → simple-name lookup fails → SEM011 on the entire declared type. The local face escaped because `VarDeclStmt` is validated by a different path (§249) that walks the parsed type tree.

**Fix (additive):** only a TOP-LEVEL arrow (depth 0 in `<>`/`()`) is the connective — nested arrows are validated recursively through the generic branch. Side effect (for the better): the genuine face `((Int) -> Int) -> Int` now also validates correctly (pre-fix the inner arrow poisoned the parse). Truly-undefined names keep failing (control `List<NoSuchType>` still SEM011 — `DeclaredTypeValidationE2ETest` 14/14 unchanged).

**Proof:** `FnTypeInGenericDeclaredTypeTest` 5/5 — verbatim face A EXECUTES `10` (CLI oracle measured), face B (field + `Void` return) builds and runs, Map/mixed face EXECUTES `6\n0` (measured), control: undefined inner type stays rejected, gate compiles A on NATIVE+JS. Q0: pre-fix checkout of `MemberResolver` → 4/5 RED. Full neighbor battery before commit: 73/73 green (`DeclaredTypeValidation`/`UndeclaredVarType`/`NestedFnTypeArity`/lambda/functions suites).

## §288 — #396: type-variable inside a FUNCTION-TYPE signature (`(T) -> T`) — ✅ FIXED 22/09 (lane 9093, `D-RULE6-BATCH` option (b): parse-time `TypeVariable` single source + interim SEM085 rejection; the complete generic-fn lowering is the 1.0-line erasure ABI — §271)

**Measured on tip (18/09, lane compiler `.22`).** Reproducer: `class Pipeline<T> { mapItems(transform: (T) -> T): Pipeline<T> {...} }` + `p.mapItems((x: Int) -> ...)` → `:0:0: error: Argument 1 of 'mapItems': expected 'function' but got 'function' [SEM014]` (self-contradictory — both sides ARE functions).

**Layer 1 (checker) — root proven by instrumentation.** `MemberResolver.declaredTypeUnresolved`/`resolveType` handle a bare type-param `T` at the TOP (scope.resolve → `TypeVariable`), but any composition that delegates to `Type.of` is scope-blind: inside `(T) -> T` the `T` lands as `ClassType["", T]` (printed by the DBG probe: `FunctionType[parameterTypes=[ClassType[, T]], returnType=ClassType[, T]]`). The call-site check compares that against the concrete `(Int)->Int` and fails. An additive checker fix was built and measured GREEN on the SEM014 (top-level-arrow-aware + `substituteFormals(receiver type-args)` + substitution descent into `FunctionType`, preserving `className`).

**Layer 2 (lowering) — why the checker fix ALONE cannot ship.** With layer 1 fixed the program COMPILES and then dies at runtime: `NoClassDefFoundError: T` (Pipeline face) / `NoSuchMethodError: kof.Function1_CT_CT.invoke(Object)` returning `T` (minimal `Box<T>.useTwice((T)->T)` face). Root: the lambda/SAM synthesis (`CompilerLambdaClass.lambdaInterfaceType`, :196) and the body-local typing path (driver `toType`, not `resolveType`) re-read the declared type from the SAME scope-blind source, so the synthetic SAM interface is mangled from `ClassType T` (`C`+name → `CT`) and its `invoke` descriptor is emitted as `LT;` — a phantom class reference. A plain generic member WITHOUT fn-type (`get(): T`) works end-to-end (measured `3`) — the disease is exactly "type-param nested inside a compound declared type".

**Decision (rule 6, stop-condition 1):** shipping layer 1 alone converts a loud compile-time error into a silent-until-load crash — forbidden (Q0/Q7, R6). The real fix is ONE type-resolution path that carries the type-parameter scope through ALL composite forms (fn-type params/return AND generic type-args `Pipeline<T>`), used by checker AND lowering — a contract change in the type pipeline, not a local edit. Needs the maintainer's nod on the approach (candidates: (a) resolveType-style deep scope-aware parser used everywhere; (b) parse-time annotation of type-param names into TypeVariable when inside a generic owner). Plan lands as this section; attack = lane compiler `.22` AFTER the decision.

**Proof of the analysis (all measured, not guessed):** instrumented probe outputs above; the three checker-side patches were validated green then REVERTED from the working tree (zero half-fix in `beta-0.4.0`); reproducers kept at the issue thread (#396) — `Pipeline` verbatim + `Box.useTwice` minimal + `Box.get` control.

**River:** same water as §271 / Cluster A (#363/#365/#366/#385/#399/#295) — type-variable erasure across composite declared types. §288 is the FUNCTION-TYPE face of that river (checker layer documented here; one design answer should cover both layers).

**Fix (22/09, lane 9093 — `D-RULE6-BATCH` option (b), maintainer vote 21/09).** Two parts, the decision's exact contract:
1. **Parse-time `TypeVariable`, single source of truth.** `TypeParams.rewrite` now recurses into `FunctionType` (params + return, nested) and `WildcardType` (bound) — the one rewrite point both `MemberResolver.resolveType` (checker) and `CompilerTypes.resolveWithTypeParams` (lowering) pass through, so the declared `(T) -> T` resolves to `FunctionType[TypeVariable(T,bound), TypeVariable(T,bound)]` everywhere: the phantom `ClassType("","T")` leaves, the `Function1_CT_CT` mangle and the `LT;` descriptor are gone (the synthetic interface erases to `Function1_O_O`). `TypeChecker.isAssignable` gained the component-wise fn×fn rule (erasure: a TV component accepts any concrete type), and `CompilerLambdaClass` preserves a `TypeVariable` return through the string round-trip instead of fabricating `ClassType("","T")`.
2. **Interim rejection SEM085 (R6).** MEASURED with the single-source fix alone: the #396 verbatim compiles clean and then dies at LOAD with `IncompatibleClassChangeError: Class Lambda0 does not implement the requested interface kof.Function1_O_O` — the call-site lambda is synthesized against its CONCRETE self-inferred signature (`Function1_int_int`) while the dispatch uses the ERASED declared one. Contextual lambda synthesis against the erased signature (+ box/unbox in the body) is the complete erasure ABI = the **1.0-line** work (§271(B)). Until it lands, `DeclaredTypeChecker.reportCompositeTypeParam` rejects any declared type whose FUNCTION carries an owner type-parameter (`(T) -> T`, `(Int) -> T`, `List<(T) -> T>` — any depth) with **SEM085** at compile, on every target (shared frontend, rule 5). Non-fn shapes with `T` (`T value`, `Pipeline<T>`, `List<T>` — the §355/§356/§357 river) stay legal and were re-verified.
**Proof:** `FnTypeVarSignatureE2ETest` 9/9 — #396 verbatim → SEM085 (not SEM014, no load crash) on JVM+Native; `Box.useTwice`, the generic-function face, `(Int) -> T` and `List<(T) -> T>` → SEM085; controls green: plain `T get(): T` (JVM/Script/JS/Native byte-parity), concrete `(Int) -> Int` fn-type (4 targets — no SEM085 false positive), `List<T>`-without-fn compile (JVM+Native — no false positive), `Zebra` inside a fn-type → SEM011 (unresolved names not masked). **Side-finding (catalogued, pre-existing, NOT this fix): §444** — generic class with a T-ARG constructor runs silent on Native (measured identical on clean origin `8a691ecc`); routed to the nat lane (CLOSED there 23/09 — §444).

## §289 — same-named static+instance fields with DIFFERENT JVM descriptors (`static Int a` + `Long a`) — ✅ CLOSED 18/09 BY THE STRICT §290 GUARD (never worked on ANY target — no `wantStatic` overload needed)

**Found hunting #294 (18/09, measured both sides of the guard).** The #294 guard (SEM076) only fires on TRUE JVM duplicates (same name + same erased descriptor). The legitimate pair `static Int a` + `Long a` still passes the guard (correctly) and then breaks downstream:
- **JVM:** compiles clean; at load `VerifyError: Bad type on operand stack … @28: getfield` (the symbol map keyed by NAME makes `classScope.define` overwrite: the static access gets the instance symbol or vice-versa).
- **JS:** compile-time ICE `KofJS: unknown local slot 0` (COMP002) — an ICE is never valid (R6).
- Pre-existing: re-measured with the guard STASHED (same two failures at tip `d0bbfdde`) — NOT caused by the SEM076 commit.

**Pointer for the fix:** field symbol lookup must disambiguate by staticness (receiver `Type.ClassType` + instance receiver vs `ClassName.member` static access are already distinguished in the call typer — the field path must carry the same bit through `classScope.define`/`resolveFieldInHierarchy`). Reproducer in `DuplicateFieldGuardTest` (same-name different-descriptor control — currently asserts the guard does NOT fire; flip it to EXECUTE when this one is fixed).

**CLOSED THE SAME SESSION, root-first (measured all four targets before deciding):** JVM `VerifyError` @getfield; JS compile ICE `unknown local slot 0`; SCRIPT printed the CLASS TYPE toString (`ClassType[packageName=, name=Ok...].a` — literal garbage in plain stdout); NATIVE compiled and RAN returning `3530822633505786184` for `Ok.a` — a pointer-like number, the WORST face (silent). No target ever executed this shape correctly, so the strict §290 guard (ONE field per NAME, any descriptor — javac's own rule) kills all four broken emissions loudly and removes the need for the `resolveFieldInHierarchy(cls, name, wantStatic)` overload entirely: no field pair reaches the resolver clobber path anymore. `DuplicateFieldGuardTest` control flipped to EXECUTE-the-rejection (5/5; Q0: descriptor-only guard = the C face compiles = RED).

**Reconnaissance 18/09 ~06:4x (this lane, faces measured — superseded by the paragraph above):** three access forms of the legitimate pair (`static Int a` + `Long a`) were mapped end-to-end on the JVM: `Ok.a` from `main` emits `aload_0; getfield` (@12 VerifyError — static access got the INSTANCE symbol: resolver returns the FIRST match by name); the bare `a` inside `showA()` and `o.a` mirror the same ambiguity. Helpers the fix will reuse ALREADY EXIST: `SemanticAnalyzer.currentMethodStatic` (from #345) decides the bare path, `FieldSymbol.accessFlags` carries the STATIC bit (#331), and the call-typer receiver split (class-identifier = static vs instance expr = dynamic) is established. Implementation = one overload `resolveFieldInHierarchy(cls, name, wantStatic)` + threading at the field sites (`ExpressionLowerer:87`, `CompilerEmission2:121/:139`, `SemExpressionTyper:391`, `ExpressionAssignmentLowerer:22`, `CompilerCaptures:188`) with the DEFAULT kept at today's first-match (r1: single-field classes unchanged); JS ICE `unknown local slot 0` rides the SAME shared IR (one fix, two targets + script interpreter parity check).

## §290 — `static Int n` + `Int n` (one class) passed every check and emitted TWO fields `n:I` → class died at load `ClassFormatError: Duplicate field name` — ✅ FIXED 18/09 (lane compiler `.22`, #294)

**Root cause:** no guard existed on the JVM FIELD namespace — JVMS §4.5 forbids duplicate `(name, descriptor)` field entries; staticness does NOT separate the namespace (the #264/SEM061 lesson for methods, applied to fields). `defineClassMembers` defined both symbols and the backend emitted both.

**Fix (additive, shared analyzer, STRICT — land form after the §289 faces were measured):** `checkMemberSignatureDupes` walks fields with key `"F:" + name` — ONE field per NAME per class, ANY type (javac's own rule, and the §289 measurements proved no target ever executed a same-name pair: JVM VerifyError, JS ICE, script/native literal garbage) — reporting **SEM076** at the second declaration, POSITIONAL (`Main.kf:3:12`, not `:0:0`). Hierarchy shadowing (`Base.v`/`Child.v`) stays legal (different member lists, measured `shadow`/`1` runs). The strict form absorbed §289 (closed at root) and made the planned `wantStatic` resolver overload unnecessary.

**Proof:** `DuplicateFieldGuardTest` 5/5 — verbatim #294 rejected with SEM076 + line>0; static×2 rejected; the Int/Long "JVM-legal" pair REJECTED (control flipped to execution of the error, §289); hierarchy shadowing untouched; the SAME diagnostic fires on JVM/NATIVE/JS (shared pass, rule 5). Q0 twice: no-guard → 3/5 RED; descriptor-only guard → the C face compiles (RED). Full `kof-compiler` battery after the strict change: **2185/0F/0E/199-skip** (zero users of same-name fields).

## §291 — `spawnWorkerThrowPropagatesThroughSelectAnyNative` reopens under full-suite load after `8b05e01b` (CI Build+Tests red 4/4 SHAs since; 0/5 before) — ✅ FIXED 18/09 (lane nat `192.168.100.17`) — TWO root causes (racy test shape + a real JVM parity bug)

**Reported by:** docs/bugs lane (.15) at `bc77f0eb`; fixed and closed by the nat lane (.17).

**Root cause (a) — the test shape is a race, not a runtime regression (measured).** The old shape spawned `falha(){throw "boom"}` and `rapida(){return 7}` — BOTH complete in µs, so the assertion pinned the outcome of a `pthread_create`-vs-scan race: the contract of `selectAny` (JVM oracle = `CompletableFuture.anyOf`) is "first to complete **in time**", with no argument-order tie-break (`docs/language-reference/concurrency.md` defines no tie-break). Measured on the same ELF: **13/200** `ok=false` on idle host (~6.5%), **~8/360** under 6-way parallel load; **JVM oracle: 100/100 `ok=false`** on the same shape — the old expectation contradicted the oracle. The x86 `kof_select_any` asm (`runtime/RuntimeConcurrency.java:461`) and the riscv one (`nat/NativeRiscvAsmRtB48.java:189`) were **read and exonerated**: forward argument-order scan, `mfence` before the read, exception priority on rethrow. The "blob layout shifted timing" hypothesis is **rejected as the fix target**: it is a symptom — a layout shift moves the luck of a racy test; the race itself is the bug, and "timing-neutral text placement" would leave the race in the tree and guarantee a reopen on the next blob change. Every sibling in the family (`selectAnyJvm`, `selectAnyNative`, `selectAnyPrimitiveJvm`, `selectAnyWaitPathReturnsValueAfterUsleep`) already pins a deterministic winner (a sleep on the loser); only this one relied on luck.

**Root cause (b) — REAL JVM bug found by the new parity test.** `kof_select_any` (`jvm/JvmRuntimeCore.java:142`) called `anyOf(...).get()` without unwrapping: the `ExecutionException` propagated raw, Kof `catch (String e)` never matched, and the worker's `"boom"` **escaped to `main`** (exit ≠0, Java stack trace) — unlike `kof_await` (`:149-156`), which rethrows the original cause. The path was never pinned: zero JVM tests existed for throw propagation through spawn (native-only coverage — the untested Q4 edge where the bug lived). Fix: the same unwrap as `kof_await` (RuntimeException/Error rethrown as-is, anything else wrapped in its cause). **Additive, semantics unchanged**: it aligns selectAny with the already-documented await behavior; the old behavior was a hard crash, which no program can depend on.

**Proof (same commit).** (i) the native test now pins a deterministic winner (the loser does `time.sleep(20)` before returning) — the same contract is still asserted (completed exceptional handle rethrown; the value-wins branch stays covered by the siblings above); (ii) new parity test `spawnWorkerThrowPropagatesThroughSelectAnyJvm`: **RED** on the old runtime (measured `ExecutionException: RuntimeException: boom @ kof_select_any` trace) → **GREEN** with the unwrap; (iii) stress on the new native ELF: **0/200** idle + **0/300** under 6-way parallel load (old shape: 13/200 idle); (iv) `KofConcurrency2Test` **44/44**. The `1f544a9b..8b05e01b` bisect that was asked is not needed: direct measurement (repro rates + oracle comparison + asm exoneration) identified the cause; §252/§286 mechanisms are not involved in these reds (the CI sibling-§286 question stays open for whoever has the web logs).

**Status.** ✅ FIXED 18/09 — closed with measurements. Related: §252 (closed, neighbor), §256(b) (closed, same family), §286 (sibling), §272/§292 (lineage of `8b05e01b`/`5f39f8ea`).
## §292 — `kof_sec_random_hex` (x86_64 security runtime) allocated `n+25` but wrote `24 + 2n + 1` bytes — heap header overflow on every 16-byte ID (requestId/traceId/correlationId) — ✅ FIXED 18/09 (lane nat `192.168.100.17`, found while porting face (c) to riscv)

**Root cause (measured, arithmetic + allocator source):** `runtime/RuntimeSecurity11.java` `kof_sec_random_hex` did `leaq 25(%rbx), %rdi` (`n+25`) before `call kof_alloc`, while the in-place hex expansion writes 2 bytes per input byte at `str+24` plus the NUL — **24+2n+1** bytes. For `n=16` (every W3C/request ID): 57 needed vs 48 granted (the riscv/x86 allocator rounds to 8B), so bytes 48–56 landed on the **next arena block's header** (`size` fully + the LSB of the free-list `next` pointer). Symptom is latent today only because the bump path re-initializes the header immediately after (self-heal); a free-list block in that slot gets its `next` overwritten by an ASCII hex byte → allocator list corruption under GC/free pressure. The comment above the instruction literally said "alloc n + 24 + 1" — the `×2` for hex was missing in the code, not in the intent.

**Fix (root):** `leaq 25(%rbx,%rbx), %rdi` (= 2n+25). The riscv64 port (`NativeRiscvAsmObs`, §272 face (c)) got the corrected formula from day one. JVM/JS are unaffected (Java/Graal string builders).

**Proof:** contract pinned by `KofObservabilityTest` (ID lengths 32/32/16 + handle 48 + JSON substrings matching the handle) on JVM + x86 native + riscv64 + aarch64 — 12/12; full suite green (see §272 face (c) tally). Honest limitation (Q3): the corruption window is not observable deterministically from pure Kof source on the bump path (that is what "latent" means); the fix is proven by the write-range arithmetic and the allocator's rounding rules, and the regression tests now prevent any size-formula change from shipping silently.

## §293 — JS `kofUiWindowSetSize`/`kofUiWindowClose` declared the handle parameter as `window`, shadowing the global that holds `__kofWindows` — every `w.size(...)`/`w.close()` was a silent no-op (issue #440) — ✅ FIXED 18/09 (docs/bugs lane)

**Found:** 18/09 ~14:25 UTC via issue #440 (`run --target js`: `w.size(400,400)` "does not persist"). The issue is a REAL bug by the rule-8 cross-check: `learn/35-kof-ui` documents `w.size(largura, altura)` ("sizes the window content") and `w.close()` — the runtime disobeyed its own docs.

**Root cause (static + measured).** In `JsRuntimeCore.java` the two functions took `function kofUiWindowSetSize(window, width, height)` / `(window)` — the handle is a NUMBER (id returned by `kofUiWindowNew`), so inside the body `window.__kofWindows` read a property off a number = `undefined` → `winEl` never found → the CSS assignment never ran; `window.resizeTo` threw `TypeError` caught and swallowed by the existing `try/catch`. `kofUiWindowClose` deleted nothing (`delete number.__kofWindows[id]` = no-op). The sibling `kofUiWindowBind` got it right with `globalThis.window.__kofWindows[win]` — the fix mirrors that pattern (no contract change: handles stay numeric ids; browser path unchanged where it already worked: `document.title` via `SetTitle` was fine, which matches the reporter's "title is not a problem").

**Reproduction before → after.** Before: headless node probe on the emitted `kof-runtime.mjs` printed `MISSING` / `after-close:still`; the regression test fails on the old code (`Tests run: 1, Failures: 1`). After: `400pxx300px` / `after-close:gone`; `WindowE2ETest` 4/4 green (3 pre-existing + `windowSizeAndClosePersistOnHeadlessDom`). Lowering was verified correct first (`Default.mjs` contains `kofUiWindowSetSize(w, 400, 300)`), so the fix is purely runtime-body.

**Scope of edit.** `kof-compiler/src/main/java/dev/kof/compiler/js/JsRuntimeCore.java` (two function bodies, parameter renamed `win` + registry via `globalThis.window`) + `WindowE2ETest` (+1 headless-DOM regression test with the node-probe technique — note for future UI JS tests: `kofUiWindowClose` is tree-pruned from the bundle unless the program calls it; the test program does). No other `window.` misuse found: `kofUiWindowNew/SetTitle/SetTheme` are clean; `JsRuntimeUiWidgets` never names a parameter `window`.

**Related:** issue #440 (closed with this SHA — browser-visual confirmation welcome from the reporter). JVM/Script/Native faces keep the documented no-op handle semantics (`WindowE2ETest` class doc) — untouched.

## §294 — null-check on a primitive-valued `Map.get` compiles and dies at runtime with `NoSuchMethodError: 'java.lang.Object java.lang.Object.valueOf(int)'` (measured, tip 18/09) — ✅ FIXED 18/09 (lane `.22`: #438 landed the contract; face 2a (re-box of the `Nullable(primitive)` branch) fixed with the raw guard + 6 tests × 3 targets)

**Found:** 18/09 ~14:35 UTC, this lane, chasing the mel finding in issue #386 ("the getOrDefault idiom crashes"). Measured on the tip reactor with fresh jars, JVM.

**Repro (minimal).**
```kof
main() {
    var m: Map<String, Int> = mapOf("a", 1)
    var z = m.get("z")          // ABSENT key, primitive value
    println(if (z != null) z else 9)
}
```
Compiles clean. Runs: `Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: 'java.lang.Object java.lang.Object.valueOf(int)'` — even with the PRESENT key (`m.get("a")`) the same program dies. Annotated form `Int? z = m.get("z")` does not crash but prints `0` for the absent key (that face is #376/§278, already parked); `m.getOrDefault("z", 9)` prints `9` correctly (landed `62bd455e`, §293-adjacent).

**What the docs promise today.** `training/idioms/collections` ("Map.get returns V? for reference values… For primitive values the type stays V"): so `z` is `Int` and `z != null` is comparing a non-nullable primitive against `null` — it should be a compile diagnostic (SEM048/§289 neighborhood) or `get` should return `Int?` (that is exactly the D-NULL-INTENT decision, #278/#438). Today it compiles, the typer narrows the branch to the `int` overload and the unbox site emits `valueOf(int)` against a receiver erased to `Object` → runtime death. §39 (FIXED 10/09) closed the `println(m.get("zz"))` overload-selection instance; the null-check consumer is a NEW instance of the same root.

**Why NOT fixed here (rule 6).** Both honest resolutions change frozen semantics: (a) reject `z != null` on a primitive → breaks any program that today survives (weak but real compat); (b) make primitive `Map.get` return `V?` → the reverted 07/09 experiment (§39 analysis) shows it explodes `==`/unboxing until Nullable-primitives land atomically — which is exactly PR #438 (JVM/Script/JS atomic N1, CI green at `eaa22b57`, pending maintainer review). The correct fix is #438 landing + this repro as one of its acceptance tests; a lone `if` in the typer would mask (Q0 forbidden).

**Resolution (measured 18/09, lane `.22`).** Two faces, two steps:
1. **Face 1 (the `valueOf(int)` receiver-erasure)** — closed by **#438 landing** (`250f6207`): `Map.get/put/remove` now type to `V?`, the slot is physically boxed (`Integer`), and `emitErasureBox`/`kof_box` never receive a raw `int`. The minimal repro above prints `9` on the JVM after #438.
2. **Face 2a (the post-#438 RE-BOX)** — #438 left a NEW crash in its wake, caught by the 6 regression tests added with this entry: `boxPrimitiveBranch` (`ExpressionTyper.java:378`) guarded with `TypeMetrics.isPrimitiveType`, which **looks inside `NullableType`** — so the already-boxed `Int?` branch was boxed AGAIN, emitting `valueOf:(Ljava/lang/Integer;)` with receiver erased to `Object` → `NoSuchMethodError: Object.valueOf(Integer)` (same for `Long`/`Boolean`). **Fix:** raw guard — only a NON-nullable primitive boxes there (`branchT instanceof Type.PrimitiveType`). Fail-first PROVEN: with the old guard the 4 new ternary/switch faces are RED with exactly those signatures; with the raw guard all green. Script and JS agree with the JVM on every face (cross-target Q3).

**Tests (same commit).** `NullablePrimitiveContractE2ETest` +6: present/absent `Int`, `Long` ×2, `Bool`, switch-expression on a narrowed `Int?`, and the null-branch join (`if (z != null) z else null` stays a reference, prints `null`) — `runAll3` (JVM+Script+JS), 19/19 on the module. Related: #386 (finding origin), #376 (annotated-face), §39 (sibling consumer, fixed), §293 (JS window shadowing), §295 (relational faces of the same D-NULL-INTENT family — face (b) still open, owner `.22`).
## §300 — KofJS re-render leaked the whole previous subtree into `__kofNodes` (and its Button actions into `__kofActions`): `kofUiRender` detached only the old root element from the DOM — unbounded silent growth on every state change — ✅ FIXED 18/09 (lane UI/style, owner = 192.168.100.17)

- **Symptom (measured 18/09, found during the Phase 9 survey of
  `docs/ui/architecture.md`):** every `stateSet`/`state` write on a mounted
  `Component` left the previous view subtree registered in
  `window.__kofNodes` forever. The DOM looked correct (only the current view
  was attached), so the leak was invisible in the page — only the registry
  grew. A component whose view builds a fresh widget on every render (the
  normal case) leaks one full subtree per state change: unbounded memory and
  an ever-growing registry that every `kofUiSubtreeIds`/`window.bind` walk
  pays for.
- **Root cause:** `kofUiRender` (`JsRuntimeUiComponents.java`) removed only
  the previous ROOT element from the DOM:
  `c.el.removeChild(oldEl)` when `c.root !== rootId`. The widget constructors
  (`kofUiLabelNew`, `kofUiButtonNew`, …) allocate a NEW handle per call and
  register it in `__kofNodes`; nothing pruned the discarded handles. The
  runtime already had the correct prune (`kofUiRemoveSubtree` — DOM + registry,
  used by `Component.remove`/Router unmount) but the re-render path did not
  call it.
- **Second face (same root):** `window.__kofActions` is a SECOND global keyed
  by the same handle. A discarded `Button` kept its action closure reachable
  forever; `kofUiButtonRemove` already deletes the entry on the single-widget
  path, `kofUiRemoveSubtree` did not.
- **Repro (embedded host, pre-fix):** mount a `Component` with
  `view { Label("v=" + s) }`, then 5 `stateSet`s → `__kofNodes` has **6**
  entries (1 current + 5 leaked); with the fix it stays **1**. Measured both
  ways in the same harness (stash/restore of the one-line fix).
- **Fix:** `kofUiRender` now calls `kofUiRemoveSubtree(c.root)` when the root
  handle changes (the existing DOM + registry prune, including `_kofGone`),
  and `kofUiRemoveSubtree` deletes the matching `window.__kofActions` entry
  for each pruned node.
- **Proof:** `ComponentCoreE2ETest.rerenderPrunesPreviousSubtreeFromRegistry`
  (asserts `nodes=1` after 5 re-renders) and
  `ComponentCoreE2ETest.rerenderReleasesDiscardedButtonActions` (asserts
  `actions=1`); both RED pre-fix (measured 6/2) and green post-fix.
  Neighbors green: `ComponentCoreE2ETest` 21/21, `UiE2ETest` 29/29,
  `KofJsBrowserE2ETest` 28/28 (real Chrome), `RouterE2ETest` 4/4,
  `UiStyleCssE2ETest` 10/10.
- **Scope:** JS-only by nature (the registry is the KofJS DOM engine; JVM and
  Native are documented no-ops). No API change, no contract change — pure
  leak fix, additive backward compatible.

## §301 — KofJS `Store.unsubscribe` was a silent no-op: subscribers were kept forever and kept receiving `set()` notifications — ✅ FIXED 18/09 (lane UI/style, owner = 192.168.100.17)

- **Symptom (measured pre-fix, embedded host):** subscribe a lambda to a
  `Store`, `unsubscribe` it with the SAME handle, then `set()` → the callback
  still fired (`log = "n=1,n=2,n=3,"` instead of `"n=1,n=2,"`). Silent
  subscriber leak on every unsubscribed store — and the documented Phase 8
  §2.6 contract ("cleanup no unmount") had no working primitive.
- **Root cause:** `kofUiStoreSubscribe` (`JsRuntimeUiEvents.java`) pushed the
  WRAPPER (`kofUiRunFn(fn)` = `fn.invoke.bind(fn)` — a NEW object per call)
  into `st.subs`, while `kofUiStoreUnsubscribe` searched the RAW Kof handle:
  `st.subs.indexOf(fn)` could never match, the `i >= 0` guard silently swallowed
  the failure, and the subscription stayed alive.
- **Fix:** subscriptions are stored as pairs `{ raw: fn, f: wrapper }`; `set()`
  notifies `sub.f`, `unsubscribe()` matches by `sub.raw === fn` identity and
  removes exactly one occurrence (first). An unsubscribe of a never-subscribed
  handle stays a no-op (listener-list semantics). Same identity contract as
  `mq.unsubscribe` (proved for JVM/Native by `KofMqE2ETest.unsubscribeStopsDelivery`).
- **Proof:** `ComponentCoreE2ETest.storeUnsubscribeStopsDelivery` — RED pre-fix
  (`expected <n=1,n=2,> but was <n=1,n=2,n=3,>`, measured by stashing the fix)
  and green post-fix; `ComponentCoreE2ETest` 22/22. JVM/Native keep their
  documented Store no-ops (the test asserts `""` there too).
- **Scope:** JS-only (the Store observable lives in the KofJS runtime; JVM
  no-op documented, Native no-op). No API change, no contract change — the
  fix only makes the existing `unsubscribe` do what it always claimed.

## §302 — Bare `List`/`Set`/`Map` in a FIELD declared type parses as `ClassType("", name)` — the class silently breaks at runtime (R6): §302 — ✅ FIXED 21/09 (lane bugs-and-gaps — CLOSEALL batch, medidas frescas; raiz já fechada pelo #443/§373)

- **Symptom (measured 18/09, two paths, zero script involvement for the
  first):** (1) compiled `.kf`: `class Box { static List items = listOf(1, 2,
  3) }` + `main() { println(Box.items.size) }` → runtime
  `java.lang.NoSuchFieldError: Class Box does not have member field
  'List items'` — the class file emits a field whose descriptor and the
  access site disagree (`CompilerTypes.toType` pins `List`→`BuiltinTypes.LIST`
  only under `allowBuiltinPins`, and the field path reaches the
  `new Type.ClassType("", typeName, List.of())` branch); (2) KofScript
  `var items: List = listOf(1,2,3)` + `println(items.size)` → interpreter
  falls to `KofInterpreterMembers.loadField` reflection → `InaccessibleObjectException: Unable to make field private int java.util.ArrayList.size
  accessible`. Either way a program that LOOKS legal (bare collection type
  also parses fine for LOCALS — `R-local-bare-List` probe was green) dies
  only at runtime, with no diagnostic: R6 violation.
- **Root cause (narrowed, not fixed):** the pin guard `allowBuiltinPins` is
  computed from `unitDeclaresType || sa.getClass(name)`; for the simple names
  `List`/`Set`/`Map` the symbol table already registers BUILTINS, so
  `userDeclares` evaluates true and the pin is skipped on the field path
  (`resolveWithTypeParams` → `toType(name, unit, sa)`), while the local-var
  path reaches the pin. A `List<Int>` (with type args) is unaffected (the
  name never equals the pin string — it goes through `Type.of` and comes out
  `ClassType("kof","List",...)` correctly, proven by `W-top-size`/`Y-top-forin`).
- **Workaround (documented, idiomatic):** always write the element type —
  `List<T>`/`Set<T>`/`Map<K,V>` — which is already the corpus form
  (`training/idioms/collections.md`). The kofscript wrapper now infers
  element-typed globals for un-annotated `var`s (`ScriptGlobalTypes`, 18/09),
  so `.ks` users hitting this must have written the bare type explicitly.
- **Not fixed here because:** the correct root fix touches the pin guard
  semantics shared by all 4 backends (typer contract — rule 6 territory
  needs the full compiler suite to land safely). Minimal repros above are
  deterministic; fix = compiler-core unit with `Type.of`/`toType` parity
  matrix (locals × fields × params × records) + this test.
**Re-procedure (2a, 18/09 ~13:20 — post `#438` merge `250f6207`, fresh jars on tip):** the crash MOVED, it did not die. Case 1 (absent key, original repro) now runs clean: `9` ✅ — the D-NULL-INTENT `T?`-via-API path holds. Case 2 (PRESENT key):

```kof
var m: Map<String, Int> = mapOf("a", 1)
var a = m.get("a")
println(if (a != null) a else -1)   // java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: Object.valueOf(Integer)
```

compiles clean and dies at the SAME `Object.valueOf(...)` family, now at the narrowing use-site (measured `P.kf:4`, stack verbatim). NOT Int-only — the present+null-check face breaks for EVERY primitive value type: `Long`/`Double`/`Boolean` die identically (`NoSuchMethodError Object.valueOf(java.lang.Long/Double/Boolean)`, `T.kf:4`); `Float` dies one step EARLIER (`ClassCastException: class java.lang.Double cannot be cast` at `T.kf:3` — the map itself stores a Double, a distinct second bug worth noting); only reference values (`String`) survive the null-check (`k` ✅). Plain `println(a)` on the same Int map prints `1` ✅ (no null-check → no bogus call). Script face: all 4 cases (absent/present × Int/String) print `9/1/v/none` ✅. So #438 fixed the ABSENT face and the PRESENT×primitive face (all primitives) is still broken — same boxing/erasure family as §270/§271/§280 (the typer emits `boxed → Object.valueOf(boxed)` at the `!= null` consumer instead of using the already-boxed value). Acceptance for the close: present+null-check × {Int,Long,Double,Boolean,String} × {JVM,JS} green, the 4-case script matrix green, original absent repro still green; the Float storage bug is adjacent (note for `.22`, possibly its own §NNN when attacked).

**Status.** ✅ FIXED 21/09 (CLOSEALL batch — TODAS as faces re-medidas VERDES no tip atual; registro fechado abaixo — crash MOVED, not dead; see re-procedure 2a; remains owner = `.22` erasure/boxing cluster, NOT #438 — that landed and fixed the absent-face).

## §295 — D-NULL-INTENT **relational operator** (`<` `>` `<=` `>=`) over a **nullable primitive** miscompiles on the JVM — (a) as an `if`/`while` **condition**: `if_icmp*` fed the boxed `Integer` → `VerifyError` at class LOAD ✅ FIXED 18/09 (lane `.18`, maintainer-directed); (b) the **boxed-local writer cluster** (literal init / default / assign / compound / increment storing primitives into `Nullable(primitive)` ASTORE slots): `integer not assignable to reference` at LOAD ✅ FIXED 18/09 (lane `.22`, same commit as `NullablePrimitiveContractE2ETest` 26/26)

**Found:** 18/09, discovered while closing §279 (the §279 else-if verbatim is exactly face (a)) and re-measured on the tip with `env -i java` (the raw `VerifyError` was being masked as a spurious "JavaFX components not found" by a polluted `JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS` in the shell — the real cause only shows with a clean env; R6: don't trust the mask).

**Face (a) — condition path (✅ FIXED).** Repro (verbatim, same as §279's else-if):
```kof
String probe(Int? v) {
    if (v == null) { return "n" } else if (v > 0) { return "e" } else { return "z" }
}
main() { println(probe(5)) }
```
Compiles clean on JVM; running it dies at class LOAD with `java.lang.VerifyError: Bad type on operand stack … Type 'java/lang/Integer' (current frame, stack[0]) is not assignable to integer`, `Default/Main.probe(Ljava/lang/Integer;)Ljava/lang/String; @22: if_icmpgt`, `stack { 'java/lang/Integer', integer }`. The `v > 0` is a **condition** → lowered via the comparison fast path, which emits `if_icmpgt` straight onto the stack — but the `Int?` local/param arrives **physically boxed** (`Integer`, per #278 Commit B) and the fast path never unboxed it before the integer compare. Even `probe(null)` (where `v > 0` is dead) fails, because the verifier checks the whole method at LOAD.
- **Root cause (measured):** `CompilerComparisons.emitComparisonShortcut` (used by `StatementLowerer.IfStmt`, the `while` and the print-if for every condition) computes `common = comparisonOperandType(...)` which **unwraps** `Nullable(Int)` → `INT`, but keeps `leftT`/`rightT` as the **`NullableType`** wrapper when emitting the operands, so `emitWideningIfNeeded(ops, leftT, common)` leaves the boxed `Integer` on the stack (the widening does no unbox) → `if_icmpgt` on a reference. The **value** path (`ExpressionBinaryLowerer.isNumericComparison`) already unboxed (`driver.emitErasureUnbox(ops, nt.inner())`, lines 288/318) — only the **condition** shortcut was missing it. `==`/`!=` over a nullable never reach the shortcut (`isComparisonShortcut` disables it there), so the bug is specific to the 4 relational operators in condition position.
- **Fix (lane `.18`, maintainer-directed — this face is normally `.22`'s D-NULL-INTENT cluster):** in `emitComparisonShortcut`, before widening/compare, unbox each operand that is a `Nullable(primitive)` via `driver.emitErasureUnbox(ops, inner)` and re-point the working type to `inner`. `emitErasureUnbox` self-gates on `needsErasureBoxing() == (target == JVM)`, so JS/Script/Native are byte-for-byte unaffected (no-op there; their relational is already correct/raw). Native's `Nullable(primitive)` stays crua per the #278 phase-2 note — the no-op is exactly right.
- **Proof:** `NullablePrimitiveRelationalConditionTest` 3/3 — else-if chain golden `e\nz\nz\nn` (probe 5/0/-3/null), plain-`if` conditions `p\nm\nz`, mixed-width `Int? >= 100000L` → `big\nsmall`; **JVM RUN + byte-for-byte JS parity**. Q0: fix stashed → 3/3 **RED** (`VerifyError` at LOAD); restored → 3/3 GREEN. Full `kof-compiler` suite **2223/0F/0E** — the shared condition path regressed nothing.

**Face (b) — boxed-local writer cluster (✅ FIXED 18/09, lane `.22`).** The recorded symptom (a `Bool big = v > 0`-style store dying at LOAD) was one face of a wider gap, re-measured on the tip via the reflection launcher (the JVM launcher masks the `VerifyError` as "JavaFX components not found" — the real error only shows when `Default.Main.main` is invoked reflectively): **Commit B (#278/#438) made the JVM local slot of a `Nullable(primitive)` a physical REFERENCE** (`storeVarOpcode`/`loadVarOpcode` → ASTORE/ALOAD, `isDoubleWidth` → 1 slot, `jvm/JvmLiteralEmitter.java:274/295`) **but never updated the WRITERS**, which boxed only when `erasesToReference(slot)` — FALSE for `NullableType` (`CompilerTypeSupport.java:89`). Every raw-primitive store into such a slot emitted `iconst/bipush … astore` → `VerifyError: Bad type on operand stack … Type 'integer' … not assignable to reference type` at class LOAD, killing even programs that never touched null. Five writer faces measured red on the tip: (b1) literal init `Int? v = 5` (`Main.main @1: astore_1`), (b2) declaration without init `Int? w` (default `0` into the ASTORE slot), (b3) simple assign `v = 9` (`@36`), (b4) compound assign `g += 1` (`IADD` over a reference), (b5) increment `v++`/`++v`. The JS/Native/Script targets ran the same programs correctly (JS `F/T`, Native ELF `F/T`) — JVM-only crash.
- **Root cause of the recorded face (b) proper** (`Bool big = <relational over Int?>`): the typer gives a comparison whose operand is `Nullable(primitive)` a `Nullable(Bool)` result, so the **local** inherits the physical-boxed-slot rule — same writer gap, face b1/b3 depending on store path.
- **Fix (lane `.22`)**: mirror the return-site D-NULL-INTENT gate (`ReturnValueLowerer`) at every writer, gating on the **CRU** primitive (`instanceof Type.PrimitiveType` — never `TypeMetrics.isPrimitiveType`, which PEEKS inside `NullableType`; re-box of an already-physical reference is the §294-2a trap, so a RHS already `Nullable` passes untouched): new `TypeMetrics.isNullablePrimitive(Type)` helper; `StatementLowerer` VarDecl (init box + no-init default now `null` — an unassigned reference slot, like `String? s;`, never a silent `0`); `ExpressionAssignmentLowerer` simple assign (box) and compound (load→`emitErasureUnbox`→binary on the INNER→rebox; null slot NPEs honestly, R6); `CompilerEmission2.emitIncrement` local path (DUP on the boxed reference, arithmetic on the inner, rebox before store — postfix leaves the OLD boxed value, prefix the new). All box/unbox emission goes through `emitErasureBox/Unbox`, which self-gate on `needsErasureBoxing() == (target == JVM)` — Script (`KofInterpreter` treats `kof_box/unbox` as identity), JS and Native are byte-for-byte unaffected; Native's `Nullable(primitive)` stays crua per the #278 phase-2 note.
- **Proof**: Q0 — 7 new tests in `NullablePrimitiveContractE2ETest` (ledger verbatim `Int? v = 5; Bool big = v > 100; Bool small = v > 0` → `F\nT`; unassigned `Int? w` → null-branch `N`; assign `9`; compound `g += 1` → `8`; `v++`/`++v` → `5\n6`; prefix + `Long?` `5000000001`; Bool-slot writer faces) **RED on the old code with the exact JVM `VerifyError`s above, GREEN with the fix — 26/26** `runAll3` (JVM+Script+JS; the one `Bool?`-slot direct-println face is pinned JVM-only, its Script read-divergence is pre-existing — measured on the OLD jar — and catalogued at §306(b)). CLI cross-target on the rebuilt jar: literal-init/compound/increment cluster prints `7\n8\n5000000001` **identically on JVM (reflection launcher), Native ELF, JS (node) and Script**. The §279 conformance-matrix 4-target cell (relational-nullable) is unblocked by this closure.
- **Original measured repro (kept for history):**
```kof
main() {
    Int? v = 5
    Bool big = v > 100
    Bool small = v > 0
    println(if (big) "T" else "F")
    println(if (small) "T" else "F")
}
```
Compiles clean on JVM; running it dies at class LOAD with `java.lang.VerifyError: Bad type on operand stack … Type integer (current frame, stack[0]) is not assignable to reference type`, verifier frames `full_frame(@48,{Object#42,Integer,Integer,Integer}, …)` — the `Bool big`/`small` locals were allocated as **boxed `Integer` REFERENCE slots** (locals show three `Integer`s after the args), so storing the comparison's primitive `int` (0/1) into them is an `astore` of an `int` → reject. This is the **declaration/store** typing layer, NOT the condition shortcut fixed in face (a): a relational whose operand is `Nullable(primitive)` produces a result the `VarDecl` path treats as a boxed reference instead of a primitive `Bool`. Same `.22` erasure/typing cluster as §294 (present×primitive null-check dying at `Object.valueOf`) and the §241 "boxed half-landed" family. Left to `.22` with this measured repro. Cross-target for face (b) not asserted here.

**Status.** ✅ face (a) FIXED 18/09 (condition shortcut, `CompilerComparisons.emitComparisonShortcut`, `NullablePrimitiveRelationalConditionTest`). ✅ face (b) FIXED 18/09 (`.22` writer-side boxing cluster — `TypeMetrics.isNullablePrimitive` + `StatementLowerer`/`ExpressionAssignmentLowerer`/`CompilerEmission2`, `NullablePrimitiveContractE2ETest` 26/26 + CLI 4-target `7\n8\n5000000001`). The §279 `conformance-matrix.md` 4-target cell (relational-nullable) is unblocked. Reader faces of the same Commit-B half-landing (JVM truthiness `if (b)` over a boxed `Bool` slot; Script printing `Bool?` locals as `1/0`) were NOT fixed here (pre-existing, measured on the old jar) and are catalogued at **§306** (owner `.22`).

## §298 — `kof deploy --target js` packages a release that cannot run (entry without its runtime)

**Found:** 18/09 ~17:00, measured on tip `235061b3` (X9 slice 3) with fresh jars.

**Status.** ✅ FIXED 18/09 (same commit as this entry — `CmdDeploy` copies the import
closure of the JS entry + `CmdDeployTest.jsFacePackagesEntry` hardened to RUN node).

**Symptom (verbatim):** `kof deploy App.kf --target js --output out` produces
`out/deploy/App-0.0.0/App-0.0.0.mjs` + `RELEASE.md` (which tells the user
`run: node App-0.0.0.mjs`). Copying the release dir to a clean location and running
the promised command dies: `Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module
'.../kof-runtime.mjs'` — the generated entry does `import { kofPrintln } from
'./kof-runtime.mjs'`, and `kof-runtime.mjs`/`kof-runtime-io.mjs` live **next to the
entry in the build dir** (`JsArtifactWriter.writeRuntime`) but were never copied.

**Root cause (read in code):** `CmdDeploy` modeled every face as a SINGLE artifact
(`Files.copy(built, jarDst)`); JVM (fat jar) and NATIVE (static ELF) truly are
single-file, ANDROID is a single APK — the JS face silently inherited the
single-file assumption and shipped half a program. A **facade of a feature**
(Q7): the slice was marked "JS packaged" but the packaged unit was not runnable.

**Why the test let it through (Q5):** `jsFacePackagesEntry` asserted file existence,
SHA256SUMS over the entry and RELEASE.md text — it never executed the artifact.
The hardening now runs `node <entry>` **inside the packaged release dir** and
asserts program output (`js ok`), plus SHA256SUMS covers the runtime files.
Honest guard: `assumeTrue(node available)` — no node, no fake green.

**Proof.** RED-before (green test × old `CmdDeploy.java`, stash-measured):
`jsFacePackagesEntry:182 "runtime deve acompanhar o entry (SHA256SUMS)" FAILURE`.
GREEN-after: `CmdDeployTest` 9/9 + 1 honest skip (android w/o SDK). The old
entry-only split behavior is also proven broken end-to-end in this session
(`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` verbatim above). Fix is additive: JVM/native/android
paths untouched (no `jsDeps` entries for them).

## §299 — APK pipeline pinned `build-tools 34.0.0`: d8 (R8 8.2.x) cannot read the project's Java-21 bytecode → every real SDK run died at dex (and a relative keystore path died at CWD first)

**Found:** 18/09 ~22:15 UTC, measured in CI — `CmdDeployTest.androidWithSdkPackagesApk` went RED on ubuntu (`90ea7c34`), after `84c82139` (X9 slice 3) shipped the android face with the pipeline **never executed on any SDK host** (local = honest skip; the weak-green family, Q5).

**Status.** ✅ FIXED 18/09 — same commit as this entry (X9 lane `.15`): two root causes, both in `CmdBuild.runApkPipeline`.

- **Face (a) — `keytool` with relative paths under `ProcessBuilder.directory(projDir)`:** `CmdDeploy` passes a relative `classes/` dir; the keystore arg stayed relative to the ORIGINAL cwd → resolved twice → `java.io.FileNotFoundException` (fixed first in `90ea7c34`: `projDir.toAbsolutePath().normalize()` at the pipeline entry).
- **Face (b) — `build-tools` pinned to `34.0.0`:** its `d8` is R8 8.2.x, which rejects `class file major version 65` (Java 21 — the version `JvmBackend` emits, `cw.visit(V21)`). Measured verbatim: `Error ... kof-app.jar:Default/Main.class: IllegalArgumentException: Unsupported class file major version 65 → Compilation failed`. The pin chose an old d8 even on images that ship newer build-tools.
- **Fix (root cause, additive):** `pickBuildTools(androidHome)` = semver-descending scan for the highest dir with `aapt2+d8+zipalign+apksigner` executable; honest gate: if the chosen d8 is pre-35 and the artifact is major 65, refuse with the explicit diagnostic (`build-tools >= 35.0.0 (DEP001 environment condition)`) — never a silent dex failure, never a fabricated APK (R6/Q7).
- **Residual (decision pending, rule 6):** emitting ANDROID at **V17** (like `AndroidProjectWriter`'s pom) would make the face work on build-tools 34 images too; that changes the JVM-emitter's output contract → `docs/development/DECISIONS.md`/roadmap queue, maintainer's call — this entry carries the honest diagnostic until then.
- **Proof.** New `CmdBuildApkToolchainTest` (4/4, deterministic — no SDK needed): highest-complete-version selection (9.0.0 < 34 < 35, incomplete 36 excluded), null-when-nothing, numeric-not-lexicographic semver, the Java-21 gate + the major reader. **RED-before measured during this unit:** `classMajorOf` initially compared signed bytes (`0xFE != -2`) and the test caught it (expected 65, got 0). CI: `90ea7c34` red with the exact message above; green-after = next CI run (e2e executes when the image has a usable d8, honest skip otherwise).

## §304 — Native `Map.get` of an ABSENT primitive-valued key silently returns `0` — the D-NULL-INTENT `V?` contract (#438) is not implemented on the native backend (measured, tip `52d5b4bf`) — ✅ CLOSED 18/09 (killed by the §284-map Map-slot contract, native lane)

**Found:** 18/09 ~23:5x, this lane, re-measuring #376 for closure. Verbatim (`mapOf` + `put("x",42)`/`put("zero",0)`, printing `m.get("x")` / `m.get("zero")` / `m.get("z")`) with the fresh reactor jar, per target: **JVM `42/0/null` ✓ · Script `42/0/null` ✓ · JS `42/0/null` ✓ · NATIVE `42/0/0` ✗**. The absent key is indistinguishable from a key mapped to `0` on native — a silent cross-target divergence (Freeze rule 5) and an R6 violation (no diagnostic, no gap code).

**Root-cause area.** #438 changed the typer/`map.get` contract (returns `V?`, JVM/Script/JS); the native mapset (`NativeRiscvAsmMapset0/1/2` + x86 map runtime) predates it and its get path folds the missing-key sentinel to the primitive default instead of a null reference. The `Int?` slot representation on native is a separate open question from #438 (which declared native out of scope).

**Why NOT fixed here.** It is native-runtime code in another lane's substrate (mapset), and the honest-resolution fork (null-as-sentinel on native vs `NATIVE00x` diagnostic for primitive maps) is a design decision (rule 6). Minimal repro above; expected = JVM's `42/0/null` on all four targets, or a compile-time diagnostic when native cannot represent `null` for `Map<K, primitive>.get`. Related: #376 (closed — JVM/Script/JS faces fixed by #438 + locked by `NullablePrimitiveContractE2ETest.mapGetMissingKeyIsNullDistinctFromPresentZero`), §294, #438, NATIVE002.

## §305 — `kof fmt` corrupted escaped CHAR (and STRING) literals — round-trip broke valid code (#447) — ✅ FIXED 18/09 (same commit)

**Found:** 18/09, issue #447 (reported on Windows host; reproduced verbatim on Linux tip `d5e4221a`).

**Symptom (measured):** input `repro.kf` with `'\\'`, `'\t'`, `'\n'`, `'\r'` (all valid, `kof check` clean) → after `kof fmt` the file no longer compiles: `'\\'` (2 bytes in source) became `'\'` (single backslash = unterminated literal, LEX004) and `'\t'` became `'` + raw 0x09 TAB byte + `'`. Same root hit STRING: `"c\"d"` emitted as `"c"d"` (breaks the string into two + stray token).

**Root cause:** `KofFormatter.formatExpr` re-serialized `LiteralExpr.value()` — which holds the **decoded** value (the lexer's `readEscape` already resolved `n t r \\ ' " 0 u`) — wrapped in quotes with **no re-escaping**. The formatter prints semantic values, not source forms: every escape whose decoded form is quote/backslash/control becomes raw and invalid source.

**Fix (additive, behavior-preserving for all other literals):** `KofFormatter.escapeLiteral` re-emits exactly the escape vocabulary the Lexer recognizes (`\\ \t \n \r \' \" \0` + `\uXXXX` for other control chars); non-ASCII stays raw (the lexer accepts it; converting would be lossy churn). Applied to both the CHAR and STRING branches.

**Incidente de entrega (registrado — regra 3 de transparência):** o commit inicial `1d463c41` levou a SUÍTE nova mas NÃO o `KofFormatter.java` (um `git add -A` rodou entre o stash do VERMELHO-ANTES e a restauração do fix → o arquivo ficou de fora do commit). CI `1d463c41`/`d05c65f5` = 3 vermelhos exatos nos testes novos (o verde local era classpath stale). Correção real entregue em `33363a3f` no tip, mesma hora: o CI pegou o que eu não peguei — **CI `1d463c41` = failure (3 reds), CI `33363a3f` = SUCCESS (12/12 no mesmo job).** Lição: medir `git show --stat` do commit ANTES do push (Q2 cobre compilação, não staging).

**Proof:** `KofFormatterTest` + 4 tests (12/12). RED-before measured with the fix stashed: 3 of the 4 new tests fail on the old code (char escapes, string escapes, idempotency/reparse); the 4th (plain non-ASCII stays raw) is the over-escape guard and passes both ways. GREEN-after: 12/12; full kof-compiler module 2212/0F/0E; `check_500` OK (KofFormatter 468). Round-trip verified byte-level on the issue's repro: `'\\'` → `'\\'`, `'\t'` → `'\t'`, fmt is idempotent.

## §306 — READER faces of a `Nullable(Bool)` local left behind by Commit B (#278/#438): JVM truthiness `if (b)` → `VerifyError` (`if_icmpne` over `java/lang/Boolean`); Script prints a `Bool?` local as `1/0` while JVM/JS print `true/false` — ✅ CLOSED 19/09 (owner `.22`; sugar rewrite + interpreter canonicalization, `NullableBoolTruthinessE2ETest` 8/8 `runAll3`)

**Found:** 18/09, discovered while pinning the §295(b) writer cluster: the Bool test (`Bool? b = true; println(b); b = false; println(b)`) cleared the JVM `VerifyError` with the writer fix but the SCRIPT target answers `1`/`0` — and the earlier truthiness verbatim (`Bool? b = true; if (b) "Y" else "N"`) dies at JVM class LOAD. Both re-measured on the **pre-fix jar** (stale kof-cli, before this cluster's boxing existed): Script already printed `1` → **pre-existing, not introduced by the §295(b) fix** (R6 honest attribution; the writer fix is byte-for-byte JVM-only).

**Face (a) — JVM truthiness.** Repro: `main() { Bool? b = true\n if (b) { println("Y") } else { println("N") } }` → `java.lang.VerifyError: Bad type on operand stack … Type 'java/lang/Boolean' (current frame, stack[0]) is not assignable to integer`, frame `locals { '[Ljava/lang/String;', 'java/lang/Boolean' }`, location `Default/Main.main @10: if_icmpne`. The truthiness site (`emitConditionalJump` and the `ExpressionLowerer` ~517-521 family: load + `KofLoadLiteral(INT, 0)` + `KofConditionalJump(NE)`) treats a `Bool` operand as an int — but the Commit-B slot physically stores a `java/lang/Boolean` reference → `if_icmpne` over a reference. Same family as §295(a) (relational over a boxed slot) one layer further: **condition-position TRUTHINESS** (no explicit comparison). Reachable WITHOUT any writer fix via `m.get("flag")` on a `Map<String, Bool>` (the value arrives as a reference) — measured: `var b = m.get("flag")\n if (b)` = same VerifyError on the tip pre-#438-era. Candidate fix (same unbox-at-read pattern the comparisons/return already use — mirror `emitErasureUnbox` before the truthiness jump when the operand type is `Nullable(Bool)`; self-gated JVM, other targets unaffected; `Boolean.TRUE` reference-identity + `IF_ACMPNE` is the alternative but only if null-safety matches `if (null)` = false — design detail for the owning turn, rule-6-adjacent). NOT fixed in the §295(b) commit on scope discipline (writer cluster was already the full diff; R6: honest boundary, tracked here).
**Face (b) — Script representation.** `Bool? b = true; println(b)` → Script prints `1` (JVM prints `true`, JS/node prints `true`); plain `Bool b = true` prints `true` on all three (measured: reflective runner). The interpreter's `normalizeReturn`/collection paths canonicalize `Boolean ↔ Integer 0/1` (KofInterpreterValues:25-42, §108), but a **local `Nullable(Bool)` slot** keeps the int form → `println` prints the raw `1/0`; the second println (`b = false`) prints `0`. Cross-target divergence on a plain `Bool?` local (Freeze rule 5). Root-cause area: Script's Nullable(Bool) slot representation vs plain Bool's — decide together with face (a) (unbox/box at the same chokepoints).
**Why NOT fixed here.** Face (a) is a READ-side change on the shared condition path (touching `emitConditionalJump` semantics = contract-adjacent, rule 6: it needs the same careful unbox-gate the §295 faces got — its own unit with its own Q0 pins); face (b) is the interpreter's representation, not the JVM cluster. Both have minimal repros above; the §295(b) test file carries the JVM pins (`nullablePrimBoolWriterFacesStoreBoxed` writer-only, JVM-pinned with the §306 pointer in its comment). Related: §295, §294, #278, #438, §108.

**Fix (19/09, `.22`).** Face (a): every truthiness site now routes a `Nullable(Bool)`-typed condition through `CompilerComparisons.nullableBoolTruthinessRewrite` — the sugar `if (b)` → `if (b == true)`, reusing the §295(a)/D-NULL-INTENT null-safe VALUE path of `==` (`Nullable(T)` vs `T` boxes both sides and compares with `Objects.equals`, so `null` reads `false` — no unbox, no `if_icmpne` over a reference, no new contract: it is desugaring to an expression the language already defines). Call sites switched to the shared `emitTruthinessJump`: `StatementLowerer` (`if`/`while`), `ExpressionLowerer` (if-expression), `ExpressionPrintLowerer` (condition of the print-expr path) and the `&&`/`||` left operand (`ExpressionBinaryLowerer` — a `Nullable(Bool)` operand can reach either branch of the rewrite, so both operand sites check). **Native is deliberately excluded** (`driver.target.isNative()` returns the condition unchanged): a native `Bool?` local slot holds the raw int (the unwrap branch of `StatementLowererLocalBoxing`), so the old `NE 0` path is the correct one there and rewriting it would BREAK parity, not fix it; this host has no qemu to measure cross, and the emission for native is byte-identical to the proven tip, so the CI cross job remains the gate (R6 — an exclusion with a reason, not a silent fallback). Face (b): the interpreter carried a MIXED canonical form for bools — `KofLoadLiteral.ofBool` stores `Integer 0/1` (`KofLoadLiteral.java:21`) while the collection path (`coerceFor("bool")`) hands back `java.lang.Boolean` — so the same `Bool?` slot printed `1/0` and compared unequal to a boxed literal depending on who wrote it. The box chokepoints now canonicalize: `kof_box` with a `java.lang.Boolean` return type coerces `Number→Boolean`, `kof_unbox` with a primitive-bool return coerces `Boolean→0/1` (`KofInterpreter.dispatch`), `unboxInt` accepts `Boolean→1/0` (defense against the `unboxInt(null)`-class CCE on the interpreter's old path); predicates `KofInterpreterValues.isBoolWrapperType`/`isBoolPrimitiveType`. Because `prepareForInterpretation` pins `driver.target = Target.JVM` (`CompilerPipeline` ~348), the interpreter executes the SAME rewritten IR — which is why the two faces close together on Script.
**Proof (Q0/Q1/Q3).** New `NullableBoolTruthinessE2ETest` **8/8 `runAll3` (JVM+Script+JS)**: face-(a) verbatim repros (`if/else` both branches `Y`/`N`; if-expression `A`; `while` loop 3 iterations), the reference-arrival path from the catalog (`Map<String,Bool>` `get`: HIT + **null face** `HIT\nNO`), face-(b) verbatim (`println(Bool?)` → `true\nfalse` — Script now agrees with JVM/JS, promoting what §295(b) had pinned JVM-only), plus plain-`Bool` control and `!= null` narrowing control. The face-(a) cases are RED on the tip before this commit with the exact `VerifyError` above; face-(b) is RED (prints `1\n0`) before the interpreter canonicalization. Control `NullablePrimitiveContractE2ETest` stays **26/26**; the writer pin `nullablePrimBoolWriterFacesStoreBoxed` remains JVM-only by design (writer-side, orthogonal to the read fix). Edges covered: null slot, false slot, collection-sourced reference, loop re-entry, non-nullable control, cross-target.

**Status:** ✅ CLOSED 19/09 (faces (a)+(b), owner `.22`). Supersedes the §295(b) note "the one `Bool?`-slot direct-println face is pinned JVM-only" — Script/JS now agree with JVM, proven by the new test. Related: §295, §294, #278, #438, §108.
