## §308 — #445: enum declared in an imported package file — class emitted at the ROOT while callers reference `pkg/Name`, switch fell into the numeric branch, JS crashed on the identity form (measured on tip) — ✅ FIXED 19/09 (same commit)

**Found:** #445 (report `jonasrochasilva-prog` with a full root-cause dossier; independent
triage by the issue lane on `055a8f55`, routed to compiler lane `.22` — §308).

**Symptoms (measured, pre-fix tip):** two-file shape `src/Main.kf` (`import pkg` +
`println(ModoOperacao.SIMULAR)` / switch) + `src/pkg/Modo.kf` (`package pkg` + enum).
`kof check src` clean; `kof run src/Main.kf` → the disguised "JavaFX runtime components"
message (§149); the reflective launcher exposes the truth: **`NoClassDefFoundError:
pkg/ModoOperacao`** — `outj/ModoOperacao.class` emitted at the ROOT while `Default/Main.class`
references `Field pkg/ModoOperacao.SIMULAR` with `aload_0` (slot 0 = `args[]`);
cross-file `switch` → `VerifyError: Bad type on operand stack @ isub` (two enum references
subtracted — the switch took the numeric branch because `SwitchStmtLowerer` gated
`enumSwitch` on `packageName().isEmpty()`); Script cross-file switch →
`not an int: ModoOperacao@…`; JS: `KofJS: unexpected op in switch case:
KofConditionalJump[NE]` — measured with a CLEAN tip jar on a **same-file** enum switch:
JsSwitchParser never learned D-ENUM207's identity form (`KofBinary(EQ, ClassType)` +
`CJump(NE)`), so enum-switch-on-JS was broken for ALL enums (no test covered it).

**Root causes:** (1) `CompilerEnumLowering.lowerEnum` hardcoded the empty package (and
`CompilerPipeline` never passed `declPkg` to it, unlike class/interface/record);
(2) ~8 resolution sites assumed an enum's package is empty: `SymbolTableBuilder`
self-type, `SemExpressionTyper` yields, `ExpressionTyper`/`ExpressionLowerer`
field-access guards (`packageName().isEmpty()` → silent fallback to
`KofLoadLocal(slot 0)`), `BuiltinTypes`/`CompilerTypes` enum recognition,
static-call sites (`values()`/`valueOf()`), `SwitchStmtLowerer` detection,
`MemberResolver` switch-expr exhaustiveness gate;
(3) JS backend: switch parser only knew SUB/`kof_string_equals` forms.

**Fix (package-aware end-to-end):** central `CompilerTypes.enumTypeOf(name, sa)` (source
of truth = the registered `ClassSymbol.type()`, real `packageOf`); `lowerEnum` receives
the declaration's package; all recognition sites use the symbol table / merged-module
declarations (`currentUnit` at lowering IS the merged unit — simple-name lookup suffices);
`ExpressionLowerer`'s `aload_0` fallback is gone for class-typed receivers (honest
UNKNOWN diagnostic instead — R6); `SwitchStmtLowerer`/`MemberResolver` gates no longer
require an empty package; `JsSwitchParser` recognizes the identity form (`identityEq`,
JS `switch` already compares singletons by `===`).

**Proof:** `EnumCrossFileE2ETest` 7/7 (verbatim cross-file; `.class` lands in `pkg/`;
`==`/identity; `values()`/`valueOf()`; switch+param; same-file control; SEM062
enum×String kept) × JVM/Script/JS. Q0 pins measured RED before the fix (5/7).
Controls green: `KofEnumTest` 6/6, `KofEnumSwitchTest` 4/4, `EnumIdentityE2ETest` 6/6,
`KofSwitchExprE2ETest` 32/32, `GuardedPatternSwitchExprE2ETest` 3/3 (59/59 total).
CLI 4-target probe on the issue's exact two-file shape: **`cop\nmovido` rc=0 on JVM
(via reflective launcher — no VerifyError), Script, JS (node) and Native (ELF)**.
Full suite: see this commit's log tail (`/tmp/opencode/suite445.log`).
**Closed 18/09 (native lane, §284-map):** the Map-slot contract added with the real erasure box makes the native `get` return the boxed slot (or `null` for a miss — `kof_map_get` already returns 0 on miss; the typed path no longer folds it to `0` because the ret type is `V?` and call-site unwrapping only runs for concrete primitive rets). Measured on the §304 verbatim with the §284-map jar: x86 `42/0/null`, riscv64 `42/0/null`, aarch64 `42/0/null`, JVM `42/0/null` — four-way identical, and `m.get("zero") == m.get("z")` is `false` (0 ≠ null through `kof_box_equals`/cru-fold). Distinct-from-present-zero is now the native behavior, no diagnostic needed (the contract IS representable). Proven by `NativeErasureBoxE2ETest.mapBoxedSlot*` (`g.get("zz")` line, 11-line golden byte-identical across the 4 targets) and `KofMapSetTest` 14/14.

## §333 — cross backends (riscv64 + aarch64) print `Char` values as NUMERIC codepoints — `println(c: Char)` / `println(map.get(k))` of a `Char` map print `97`/`66` where JVM and x86 print `a`/`B` — ✅ FIXED 19/09 (branch `fix/259-nullable-primitive-native`, #259/N2 — proof measured, PR pending maintainer review; see the closure block at the end of this section) — owner = native lane

**Found:** 18/09, native lane `.17`, measuring the §284-map golden battery. Minimal repro (`/tmp`-style, 6 lines): `var cm = mapOf(); cm.put("c", 97 as Char); val k = cm.get("c"); println(k); var c: Char = 66 as Char; println(c)` → JVM `a`/`B`, x86 `a`/`B`, riscv64 `97`/`66`, aarch64 `97`/`66`.

**Root:** there is no `kof_char_to_string` in the cross runtime slices (grep: zero hits in `NativeRiscvAsm*`); the riscv/aarch `valueOf(char)` chain and the primitive println branch fall through to `kof_int_to_string`, which formats the codepoint as a number — the exact behavior §216/D-PRINT superseded on JVM+x86 (char prints the CHARACTER; the "97 (H)" numeric contract in `strings.md` is the pre-D-PRINT era). The x86 counterpart DOES route char→`kof_char_to_string` (UTF-8 encoding, §216 fix `69bc0f73`), so this is a cross-porting omission, rule 5 (the fix belongs in the riscv emitter/asm slice; aarch64 inherits via the translator).

**Not a §284 regression:** the typed-`Char` println path is independent of the box work (measured the same numeric output on plain `println(c)` with `c` a local `Char`, no map, no box). The §284-map battery merely surfaced it because `M2`'s char line became part of the 4-way md5 diff.

**Fix sketch (next native-lane unit):** port `kof_char_to_string` to a riscv asm slice (single code unit ≤ 0xFFFF → UTF-8 encode, same shape as the x86 one — surrogate-pair caution: astral `Char` = one UTF-16 unit, encode the WTF-8 lone surrogate exactly as x86 does today); wire `valueOf(char)` + the cross println primitive branch to it; golden = JVM oracle (`a`, `B`, `é`=233→`é`), tests: extend `NativeErasureBoxE2ETest` map program or a new `KofCharCrossE2ETest`. Related: §216 (closed, x86/JVM/JS faces), §104b (D-PRINT), §334, NATIVE002.

**✅ FIXED 19/09 (branch `fix/259-nullable-primitive-native`, #259/N2 — PR pending maintainer review).** Implemented exactly along the sketch above: `kof_char_to_string(a0=codepoint)` added to `NativeRiscvAsmRtB49` (1/2/3-byte UTF-8 encode, same string layout as `kof_int_to_string` — len at +16, bytes at +24, NUL-terminated), and both dispatch sites wired in `NativeRiscvCrossOps`: the `valueOf(char)` branch and the println primitive branch now emit `kof_char_to_string` instead of falling through to `kof_int_to_string`. aarch64 inherits through the translator (no per-arch code).

Proof — this section's own repro (`var cm = mapOf(); cm.put("c", 97 as Char); val k = cm.get("c"); println(k); var c: Char = 66 as Char; println(c)`), run on the three native targets under QEMU plus the JVM oracle:

| program | JVM/x86 oracle | riscv64 | aarch64 |
|---|---|---|---|
| §333 map repro | `a` / `B` | `a` ✅ | `a` ✅ |
| `println('K')` | `K` | `K` ✅ | `K` ✅ |
| `println('é')` (2-byte UTF-8) | `é` | `é` ✅ | `é` ✅ |

Also covered by the new corpus `NativeNullablePrimitiveContractE2ETest` (`Char?` null/present rows, including the `"c=" + c(true)` concatenation face) — green on JVM, Script, JS, x86-64, riscv64 and aarch64.

**Side finding — 3 cross tests were pinning the PRE-D-PRINT behavior (stale goldens, refreshed in the same front).** Enabling this fix turned them red, which is how the stale goldens surfaced: `NativeStringUtf16CrossTest` and the `nativeStringLengthAndCharAtUtf16` / `*StringMethods` methods of `NativeRiscv64E2ETest` and `NativeAarch64E2ETest` expected the **codepoint** (`233`, `55357`, `98`) for a bare `println(s.charAt(i))`. Their goldens are dated 11/09 — before §216/D-PRINT (15/09), which decided `Char` prints the CHARACTER, and **x86 had already migrated** (`NativeE2ETest.nativeStringCharAtUtf16` expects `é` for `println(s.charAt(3))` and casts the lone surrogates `as Int`, which is the better assertion — a lone surrogate is not a displayable character). The cross faces kept passing only because cross had not yet adopted D-PRINT. They are now aligned with the x86 format (commit `ef5dbeaa`). Measured before/after on the same 8-class set: 13 failures → 7 (= the base). Lesson for anyone closing a D-PRINT-shaped gap on the cross targets: the cross goldens for `println(char)` are pre-D-PRINT, and the JVM is **not** a usable oracle for the lone-surrogate rendering on a Windows host (the console charset degrades the output — `é` came out as the single Latin-1 byte `E9` and the emoji as `?`); the x86 test is the reference.

## §334 — `kof_box_equals` (introduced §284-map) treats two boxes as unequal when their raw payload words differ — the one honest divergence from `Double.equals` is the NaN case (JVM: `NaN.equals(NaN)` = true; native boxed-erasure: false) — ✅ CLOSED 21/09 (lane bugs-and-gaps — batch CLOSEALL da mantenedora)

**Found:** 18/09, while writing `kof_box_equals` (x86 `RuntimeErasureBox` + `NativeRiscvAsmRtB49`): the comparison is `(tag, payload-bits)` equality, which matches `Integer/Long/Boolean.equals` and `Double.equals` for every value EXCEPT NaN (and the signed-zero pair: JVM `Double.compare` treats −0.0≠0.0 but `Double.equals` also returns FALSE for 0.0 vs −0.0 — payload bits differ → native agrees ✓; only NaN diverges). Reachable only through `Object`/erasure slots holding `1.0/0.0`-style NaN boxes (`c.o = 0.0/0.0; c.o == c.o2`), which no test/corpus program does today.

**Options (NOT decided — rule 6 territory):** (a) leave it (document here, honest divergence, NaN-on-native-equals-NaN is a philosophy question the freeze never touched); (b) add the JVM guard `if (tag==4 && bits==0x7FF8000000000000) → equal` (matches `Double.equals`'s single special-case; canonical-NaN-pattern assumption — exotic NaN payloads (rare, not producible by Kof float ops which canonicalize via SSE) would diverge back). Cost of (b) = 4 instructions × 3 backends + 1 golden test. Not attacked here because the §284-map unit was already wide and inventing a test for an unreachable edge adds no proof value (Q3).

**Repro (current behavior, if anyone ever needs it):** `class C { Object o }` … `c.o = 0.0/0.0`?? — division-by-zero literal is a compile-time diagnostic (OBS-009), so the NaN box is NOT constructible from Kof source today (no `Double.NaN` in stdlib either) → the face is UNREACHABLE until a NaN producer exists. Downgrade to informational if a NaN producer ever lands (math library official-package plans). Related: §333, §284-map, OBS-009, DECISIONS.md (NaN policy, if ever needed).


- **CLOSED (21/09, lane bugs-and-gaps — maintainer CLOSEALL directive, vote in `DECISIONS.md` D-CLOSEALL-BATCH):** probe MEDIDO hoje nos DOIS alvos — `var n = 0.0 / 0.0` IMPRIME `NaN` (existe hoje produtor de NaN alcançável do fonte: o guard `ARITH001` só fireia em INT; float sem guard). A face box-vs-box de duas divisões imprime IDÊNTICO no JVM e no native nas quatro formas (`NaN / false / false / false`) = paridade onde alcançável. A divergência de bits (NaN-special-case do `equals` da JVM vs comparação de payload em bits) só manifesta com DOIS payloads de NaN DIFERENTES (signaling/exóticos), que nenhum código-fonte Kof produz hoje (produtor único `0.0/0.0`, canônico). Downgrade para informativo conforme o plano da própria entrada; REABRIR (guard da opção (b), pronto no texto acima) se algum produtor exótico de NaN aparecer (extern/FFI ou o pacote math).

## §337 — 7 cross tests fail with **SIGSEGV (exit 139) under `qemu-aarch64`** — `NativeRiscvDtoaTest.dtoaMatchesJvmOracleOnAarch64` plus the 5 GC classes (`GcFreeList`, `GcList`×2, `GcMark`, `GcSweep`×2) — ✅ CLOSED 19/09 (does NOT reproduce on a Linux host — WSL2-environment-specific, see the closure block; owner = native lane)

> **Renumbered §336 → §337 on 19/09** when this branch rebased onto `f7a45651`: the compile lane independently landed its own **§336** (`as`/`instanceof` precedence, #459) in the same window. Two sections cannot share a number.

**Found:** 19/09, while measuring the #259/N2 front (native nullable return/local) with the full suite under WSL2 + QEMU. Unrelated to that work: it reproduces **identically on the base** `77eaa168`.

**Measurement** — the same 8-class set, same host, same recipe (see the recipe below), so the comparison is apples-to-apples:

| | tests | failures |
|---|---|---|
| base `77eaa168` | 110 | **7** ← all `qemu-aarch64` SIGSEGV |
| branch `fix/259-nullable-primitive-native` (before the Char golden refresh) | 110 | 13 ← the 7 + 6 stale Char goldens |
| branch (after the refresh, commit `ef5dbeaa`) | 110 | **7** ← identical to the base |

Full suite on the branch under WSL2: `Tests run: 2404, Failures: 8, Errors: 0, Skipped: 36` — the 7 above plus one row of the new nullable corpus (`branchesLocalsAndForwardedReturn` on `NATIVE_AARCH64`), which is the pre-existing `Float +=` → `NaN` defect filed as #464. So the suite's remaining redness on this host is entirely pre-existing.

**Repro (each one):** run the class under `mvn -o -pl kof-compiler -am test -Dtest=<class>` on a Linux host with cross binutils + QEMU; the aarch64 binary dies with `139`:

```
NativeRiscvDtoaTest.dtoaMatchesJvmOracleOnAarch64      qemu aarch64 falhou (139)
NativeRiscvGcFreeListTest.freeListReusesSlotAndMemstatsCountsAarch64   (139)
NativeRiscvGcListTest.gcListLinksNewBlocksWithFlagsAarch64             (139)
NativeRiscvGcListTest.gcListReuseDoesNotDuplicateAarch64               (139)
NativeRiscvGcMarkTest.conservativeMarkMarksReachableAarch64            (139)
NativeRiscvGcSweepTest.longAllocLoopSurvivesArenaExhaustionViaCollectAarch64 (139)
NativeRiscvGcSweepTest.sweepRecoversDeadAndMarksLiveAarch64            (139)
```

**Scope hint (not a root cause — not investigated):** aarch64-only, and it spans *different* runtimes (dtoa/libc formatting and the GC mark/sweep/free-list). What they share is the aarch64 code path **under `qemu-aarch64`**, while riscv64 runs the analogous code fine — so the prime suspect is the cross-translator/runtime for aarch64 rather than a single runtime function. §283 (aarch64 scheduler never terminating under qemu) is catalogued separately in the same family.

**Measurement recipe (costs time to rediscover):**
1. A Windows host **without GNU `as`** cannot measure the native targets at all: every native-target test fails with `as not available ... COMP001` (~1000 diagnostics in one suite run). Native evidence needs WSL2/Linux with binutils (`as`, `ld`, plus `riscv64-linux-gnu-as`/`aarch64-linux-gnu-as` for the cross targets) and QEMU.
2. `Unresolved compilation problem: dev.kof.runtime.KofJsRunner cannot be resolved to a type` (and the same for `org.graalvm.polyglot.Context` / `[LValue;`) surfaces as a **test-execution** error, not a build error, and poisons the failure count — on the base tree it aborted discovery outright (`Tests run: 0`). `rm -rf kof-runtime/target kof-compiler/target` **before** running clears it; the same clean recipe then compiles the branch with zero such errors.
3. `-pl` **without** `-am` fails on offline dependency resolution — the suite only runs with `-am` (already recorded in DOING; the failure mode is easy to misread as a code problem).

**✅ CLOSED 19/09 (lane nat) — the 7 SIGSEGVs do NOT reproduce on a Linux host; they are WSL2-environment-specific.** Re-measured on tip `f9119550` (Linux, cross binutils + `qemu-aarch64`/`qemu-riscv64` **8.2.2**, sysroot `/tmp/opencode/x`): `mvn -o -pl kof-compiler -am test -Dtest=NativeRiscvDtoaTest,NativeRiscvGcFreeListTest,NativeRiscvGcListTest,NativeRiscvGcMarkTest,NativeRiscvGcSweepTest` → **16/16 GREEN, 0 skipped**, including ALL 7 named Aarch64 cases (`dtoaMatchesJvmOracleOnAarch64`, `freeListReusesSlotAndMemstatsCountsAarch64`, `gcListLinksNewBlocksWithFlagsAarch64`, `gcListReuseDoesNotDuplicateAarch64`, `conservativeMarkMarksReachableAarch64`, `longAllocLoopSurvivesArenaExhaustionViaCollectAarch64`, `sweepRecoversDeadAndMarksLiveAarch64`). The full 4-module suite is also green on this host (2860 tests, 0F/0E). No `nat/` commit between the report's base `77eaa168` and this tip touched GC/dtoa, so this is not a fix that landed — it is the host. Per AGENTS ("Windows hosts / Native validation: a `ToolchainMissing` / toolchain result is an environment precondition failure, not by itself proof of a Kof regression; run the gate in Linux/WSL with the toolchain available"), the WSL2 `139` is an environment defect of that host (qemu/toolchain/sysroot), not a code defect on `beta-0.4.0`; the recipe above stays as the reference for whoever can reproduce it on WSL2.

## §309 — `CmdDeployTest.publishIsHonestGapD2` RED at tip: D2-A trocou a recusa e não atualizou o próprio teste — ✅ CLOSED 19/09 (medição `.22` pegou tip pré-rebase; sem repro no tip atual)

Registrado 19/09 ~06:5x pela ISSUE-LANE `.22` (condição de parada 3: vermelho alheio não é "consertado" por quem chegou depois). **Medido no tip limpo `17cc54cf`** (clone isolado `~/tipbuild`, sem patch local, sem `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` no ambiente): `mvn -o -pl kof-cli -am -Dtest=CmdDeployTest` → `Tests run: 8, Failures: 1, Errors: 0, Skipped: 1`.

**Repro mínima:** rodar `CmdDeployTest#publishIsHonestGapD2` em ambiente sem token. **Fato:** o teste afirma que a saída de `--publish` sem token contém `DEP001`; desde o **D2-A (D-POLL-19, 19/09)** a recusa é `"--publish needs GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN (D-POLL-19/D2-A: GitHub Releases is the official host)..."` (`CmdDeploy.java:51,140`) — sem `DEP001`. ## §338 — JS backend: `&&`/`||` in **value position** leaks the operand — a nullable RHS (`Bool?` = `null`) prints `null` where the contract says `false` (#486) — ✅ FIXED 19/09 (branch `fix/486-js-logical-bool`; PR pending maintainer review — proof measured, see the closure block at the end of this section) — owner = JS lane

**Found:** 19/09, while fixing #462 (the canonical `Bool` result of `&&`/`||`). The value-position faces now hold on JVM/Script, but JS diverges when the **right** operand is a `Bool?` that is null.

**Measured** (tip `f7a45651`): `println(true && nb())` and `println(false || nb())` print `null` on JS where JVM/Script print `false`; `true && tb()` is `true` everywhere. Any consumer is affected, not just `println` — the expression's value is `null` where its declared type is `Bool`.

**Root:** `ExpressionBinaryLowerer`'s dedicated short-circuit IR block is excluded for JS (`&& driver.target != Target.JS`) — the exclusion has a recorded reason (the KofJS reconstructor moves temporaries out of a loop body → `ReferenceError`, measured 17/09). Without that block JS emits a **raw** `&&`/`||`, and JavaScript's logical operators return the **operand** (`true && null` → `null`), not a boolean.

**Not caused by the #462 fix:** in the failing case the *left* operand is already `Bool`, so the new `ExpressionTyper` rule does not enter — the `null` comes from the JS backend. Confirmed pre-existing.

**Fix sketch:** canonicalise the JS result while keeping JS's native short-circuit — wrapping in `!!` (`!!(a && b)` yields a real `Boolean`; `!!(true && null)` → `false`). Note the existing `kofBoolValueOf` is a *formatting* helper (string `true`/`false`), not a coercion. Careful: the `KofBinary` → JS IR mapping is shared with the **condition** path, where returning the operand is harmless — the coercion is correct in both, but short-circuit must stay intact.

**Status:** **not fixed** (the #462 DoD asks only that JS not regress, and it does not). Behaviour is **pinned** in `NullableBoolTruthinessE2ETest#logicalValuePositionWithNullableRhsJsGap` with a pointer here, so it cannot change silently. Filed as **#486**.

**✅ FIXED 19/09 (branch `fix/486-js-logical-bool`; PR pending maintainer review).** The fix is local to the JS backend: `JsCallEmitter.binaryExpr` wraps **only the boolean** `AND`/`OR` branches in `!!` — `!!(a && b)` / `!!(a || b)`. The native operator stays inside, so the short-circuit is untouched (`false && rhs()` never evaluates `rhs`); `!!` materialises a real `Boolean`. The bitwise paths (`&`/`|`) are unchanged, still behind the `JsTypeMapper.isBoolOperand` guard. `kofBoolValueOf` was deliberately **not** used — it preserves `null` (that is `Bool?` semantics, which is exactly what must not escape here).

Proof — Q0 first, changing **only the test golden** (no production change), on base `7d47d30a`:

```text
expected: false / true / false / false
actual JS: false / true / null  / null
```

Then the production patch:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `NullableBoolTruthinessE2ETest` | 15 run / **1 failure** | **15/15** |
| `KofJsE2ETest#logicalAndOrShortCircuit` + `#bitwiseAndOrStillWorks` (the mapping guards) | — | **2/2** |
| `NullablePrimitiveContractE2ETest` | — | 26/26 |

The test that used to pin the gap is now `logicalValuePositionWithNullableRhsJsMatchesKofContract` and asserts the contract (`false/true/false/false`) — it cannot go back to pinning the divergence. Also `KofJsE2ETest#execStdlibTimeAndIo` fails on this host, but it fails **identically without the patch** on the same clean tree and its program contains no `&&`/`||` (it is `writeFile` → `-1` / `readFile` → `null`), so it is pre-existing and unrelated.

## §336 — `as`/`instanceof` on the LEFT of a higher-precedence binary op silently dropped the operator+RHS: the type-ref was parsed by the VALUE precedence-climb and swallowed `Double / 2.0` as a malformed type → `checkcast "?"` + lost arithmetic, `NoClassDefFoundError: ?` at runtime (#459) — ✅ CLOSED 19/09 (`.22`; dedicated type-ref path + follow-on `toType`/SEM011/array-checkcast fixes, `AsCastPrecedenceE2ETest` 6/6 `runAll3`)

- **Found/registered 19/09 by PublioSantos (#459), root-caused in the issue itself** (byte dump `checkcast "?"`, no `ddiv`, `astore` right after the cast; differential sweep `+ - * / % <<` all broken cast-on-left, cast-on-right clean). Re-measured on tip `f520ea87` before touching anything: `check` → `no errors`, JVM run → `NoClassDefFoundError: ?` — exact.
- **Root:** `ExpressionParser.parseBinary` gave the RHS of `as`/`instanceof` to `parseBinary(ctx, prec+1)` — a VALUE parse. For a lone type name the recursion returned just the identifier (which is why it worked); any following operator (`/`, prec 8 ≥ 6) was consumed into the "type", and the lowerer (`IdentifierExpr` guard) saw a non-identifier RHS, kept `targetType = UNKNOWN` and emitted the `"?"` fallback — silent miscompile (R6), not a diagnostic.
- **Fix (root, not symptom):** RHS of `as`/`instanceof` now ALWAYS goes through the dedicated type-only path `TypeParser.parseTypeRef` (primitive, dotted, generics `<>`, `[]`, `?`, function type — the bug-127 LPAREN branch is subsumed, `looksLikeFunctionTypeRef` dead-code removed) and control returns to the precedence loop: `a as Double / 2.0` = `(a as Double) / 2.0` per `grammar.md` §5.1 (as=5, add=7, mul=8). Old valid shapes produce the SAME AST (`n as Int == 0`, `9 as Long as Object`, `x as List<Int>` via clean args).
- **Consequences the fixed parser made reachable (also fixed, same unit — Q7 complete):** (1) `CompilerTypes.toType` never resolved a PARAMETERIZED name (`"List<Int>"` fell to `ClassType("", "List<Int>")`) — a `contains("<")` branch now parses it via `Type.of` and qualifies the base through imports; (2) the semantic analyzer flagged the full type string as an undefined variable (`SEM011`) — `SemExpressionTyper.looksLikeTypeRefName` exempts type-ref-shaped names (the lexer never produces `<`/`[`/`?` inside identifiers), subsuming the bug-127 exemption; (3) `JvmOpEmitter` CHECKCAST/INSTANCEOF mapped everything non-ClassType to `"?"` — `castTargetName` now handles ArrayType (descriptor `[I`/`[Ljava/lang/X;`) and NullableType (inner, boxed). JS/Native ignore `KofCheckCast` (no-op) — untouched; cross e2e unchanged.
- **Proof:** `AsCastPrecedenceE2ETest` **6/6 `runAll3`** (JVM+Script+JS): verbatim `a as Double / 2.0` = `0.5`; the full `+ - * / % << >> >>>` matrix cast-on-left; cast-on-right control; `==`/`>` after cast still left-bind; `as List<Int>`/`as Int[]` end-to-end (compile + run — the JVM oracle printed `2`, not a CCE); `instanceof` + `==` control and the honest `SEM002` diagnostic when `+` now legitimately meets a Bool (pre-fix the `+` vanished into the type). Neighbors green: `ConformanceMatrixTest` 11/11 (incl. the bug-127 `castfn` 4-target cell), `ParserGarbageTypePrefixE2ETest` 9/9, cast/nullable/lambda/formatter batteries, `javac` full tree rc=0.
- **Related:** #458 (the `ExpressionBinaryLowerer` duplicate shipped by `988f8afd` — already dead since `7e7514eb`, re-verified javac-clean on the tip and closed); §306/§295 (same reader/writer family, untouched); #459 CLOSED with this unit.
## §339 — `String.format` float specifiers were **locale-sensitive** — `%.2f` printed `3,14` on a `pt_BR` host JVM, diverging from Script/JS and breaking output determinism (#466) — ✅ FIXED 19/09 (`.22`; lowering always emits `String.format(Locale.ROOT, ...)`; JS host bridge pinned too)

- **Found/registered 19/09 by PublioSantos (#466)**, measured on tip `b68b7305`: `println(String.format("%.2f", 3.14))` printed `3,14` on a `pt_BR` default-locale JVM (the lowering emitted the 2-arg `String.format(String, Object[])` overload, which is locale-sensitive by contract). `%e`/`%g`/`%+.2f`/`%5.2f` all followed the host. Script face went through the SAME IR and matched; the GraalJS runner bridge (`KofJsRunner` → `String.format(fmt, …)`) inherited the host default too — the §239 "byte-a-byte parity" promise silently depended on the machine's locale.
- **Fix (root, R10 "correct and deterministic by default"):** `StringFormatCallLowerer` now pushes `KofGetStatic(java.util.Locale.ROOT)` first and emits the real 3-arg descriptor `String.format(Locale, String, Object[])`; the JS `isStaticFormat` gate accepts the 3-arg shape and drops the Locale operand (the JS runtime formatter is locale-free by construction); `KofJsRunner.stringFormat` pins `Locale.ROOT` on the host bridge. Old 2-arg bytecode shape is still accepted by the gate (no cache-format breakage).
- **Face NOT fixed (pre-existing, catalogued here for the native lane):** Native x86/riscv/aarch have **no `String.format` implementation at all** — tip links with `undefined reference to 'java_lang_String_format'` (COMP001) for ANY float/`%d` program; the issue measured JVM only and this unit does not regress it (same honest link failure, now with one more symbol in the list). Native formatting = native-lane scope (needs a `sprintf`-class formatter in the asm runtime).
- **Proof:** `StringFormatLocaleE2ETest` **3/3** — JVM child under `-Duser.language=pt -Duser.country=BR` prints the ROOT golden (`3.14`, `1.234568e+03`, `0.000420000`, `+3.14`, ` 9.99|ab` — golden measured from a real JDK `String.format(Locale.ROOT, …)` oracle class, not memory); Script and JS-via-Graal-runner faces assert byte-equal to the same golden. **RED 3/3 pre-fix** (each face printed the comma variant), GREEN post. Neighbors: `StringFormatVarargsE2ETest` 9/9 (§239/§156 corpus unchanged — all locale-neutral specifiers), full `kof-compiler` targeted runs green.

## §341 — `class Dog(...) extends Animal` (compact-ctor = synthetic record) compiled silently and died at load with `IncompatibleClassChangeError` — the compiler never registered records as final (#470) — ✅ FIXED 19/09 (`.22`; `SEM070` at compile time, all 4 targets — shared frontend)

- **Symptom (issue #470):** `class Animal(String name) { }` + `class Dog(String name) extends Animal { }` → clean build, then `java.lang.ClassLoader.defineClass` throws `IncompatibleClassChangeError: class Dog cannot inherit from final class Animal`. Silent at compile = R6 violation (same family as §339/#469).
- **Root cause (measured):** the parser turns `class X(<params>)` into a `RecordDeclarationNode` (synthetic record) and the backend writes `ACC_FINAL` into every record's class file (javap on `Animal.class`: `flags: (0x0011) ACC_PUBLIC, ACC_FINAL`). But `SemanticAnalyzer.finalClasses` only collected explicit `final class` (§339) — and the record path (`analyzeRecord`) had **no** extends check at all.
- **Fix (additive diagnostic, freeze-safe — code that compiles AND runs is untouched):** (1) `SymbolTableBuilder.preDeclareType` registers **every** `RecordDeclarationNode` in `finalClasses` (explicit + synthetic); (2) new `ClassShapeChecks.checkRecordDeclaration` called from the record dispatch (`SemanticAnalyzer.analyzeDeclaration`): a non-null super that is a record (`ClassSymbol.superClass ∈ {"Record", *.Record, */Record}`) → `SEM070: cannot extend record 'X' — records are implicitly final; compose it (hold it in a field) or use a plain class`; a plain-final super → the §339 message. `class X extends <record>` (non-synthetic) is caught by the existing `checkSuperclass` via the registration in (1).
- **Proof:** `ClassShapeChecksTest` +3 cases (issue verbatim → SEM070 names `Animal`; `record Point` + `class Holder extends Point` → SEM070; negative control — mutable `class Dog extends Animal` with explicit `constructor` + `super(name)` and a plain `record Tag` still compile **and run**, `Rex says woof v`) — 8/8 green, `mvn -o -pl kof-compiler -am -Dtest=ClassShapeChecksTest`. CLI repro on the rebuilt jar: `x.kf:11:1: error: cannot extend record 'Animal' ... [SEM070]`, no `o/` emitted.
- **Scope note:** making compact-ctor classes extendable/mutable is a **rule 6 design decision** (frozen `class X(...)` = record contract, `training/idioms/classes.md:24`), not an agent edit — §340's routing ("the fix is a compile-time diagnostic") is exactly what shipped. Script/JS/Native share the frontend, so the diagnostic is honest on all 4 targets (parity rule 5).

## §342 — aarch64 translator: single-precision FP ran as double (`fadd.s`/`fsub.s`/`fmul.s`/`fdiv.s` → `fadd d0,…`, result read as float = `NaN`) and the int→Float cast (`fcvt.s.w`/`fcvt.s.l`) was never translated (`as` aborted) — ✅ FIXED 19/09 (nat lane; `NativeAarch64Translator`)

- **Found 19/09 by the nat lane in the Q4 hunt of the §129 port**, and the PRISTINE tip `b1c7c713` was already red: `NativeNullablePrimitiveContractE2ETest.branchesLocalsAndForwardedReturn` fails ONLY on `NATIVE_AARCH64` — `Float? x = 2.5; x += 1.0; println(x)` prints `NaN` (JVM/riscv64/x86 print `3.5`). Deterministic (3/3 local + 1/1 in a clean worktree of the remote tip). Latent since the translator was written (sibling of bug 80, which fixed `fcvt.d.l`/`fcvt.s.d`/`fcvt.d.s` and **missed** the `.s`); it only surfaced when the `Float?` path of #259/N2 started emitting `fadd.s`.
- **Root cause (face 1):** `NativeAarch64Translator` (the `fadd./fsub./fmul./fdiv.` block) did `String suffix = mn.substring(5)` — which returns `"s"`/`"d"` **without the dot** — but compared `suffix.equals(".s")`; the comparison was ALWAYS false, so every `.s` operand was emitted in a `d` register (`fadd d0, d0, d1`); the following `fmov w9, s0` read the low-32 garbage of the double → `NaN`. The `.d` ops were accidentally correct (the false branch was already `d`).
- **Root cause (face 2):** the `fcvt.` block covered `fcvt.w/l.s/d` (float→int) and `fcvt.d.w/l` (int→double) but **not** `fcvt.s.w`/`fcvt.s.l` (int→single) — it fell through and `as` aborted with `unknown mnemonic 'fcvt.s.w'` (assembler error, COMP001). `i as Float` never compiled on aarch64.
- **Fix (root, 2 lines):** `suffix = mn.substring(4)` (keeps the dot, matches `.s`); the int→float branch now accepts dest `d` **or** `s` (`scvtf s0, w0` / `scvtf s0, x0`), mirroring the int→double branch.
- **Proof:** `NativeAarch64E2ETest.aarch64SinglePrecisionFloatAndIntToFloatCast` + the `NativeRiscv64E2ETest.riscv64SinglePrecisionFloatAndIntToFloatCast` mirror, golden = JVM oracle (9 lines `4.0 / 1.0 / 3.75 / 1.6666666 / 7.0 / 3.5 / 9.007199E15 / 6.0 / 3.5`; covers single-precision `+ - * /`, `Int→Float` (`fcvt.s.w`), `Long→Float` (`fcvt.s.l`), compound `Float? +=`, loop). **Q0:** with the translator reverted the aarch test is RED (`unknown mnemonic 'fcvt.s.w'`/`'fcvt.s.l'`) and the pristine tip was red 42/1; post-fix `NativeNullablePrimitiveContractE2ETest` 42/42 and both arch E2Es green.
- **Related:** §129 (unit that exposed the bug — the per-TID port did not introduce it), bug 80 (sibling fix in the same translator), §181 (float→int cast, another face). DO NOT TOUCH: §304/§302, rule 6.
## §344 — tip gate red: `JsCallEmitter` 597→608 crossed the ≥600 CRITICAL line (`check_500` fails CI) — `09e40afb` recovery added +11 lines with no split — ✅ FIXED 19/09 (plataforma-universal frente total, diretriz mantenedora — lane nao limita)

## §343 — tip suite red (the CODEGEN bug; the 500-gate face of the same culprit is §344): `09e40afb` broke JS codegen of switch-case — `BackendParityTest.parityArrayAndSwitch` ICE `COMP002: unexpected op in switch case: KofConditionalJump[comparison=NE...]` — ✅ FIXED 19/09 (plataforma-universal frente total, `a604798a`)

- **Symptom (measured 19/09, full suite on tip):** `kof-compiler` 2491 run / **1 failure** — `dev.kof.compiler.BackendParityTest#parityArrayAndSwitch`: the array.kf fixture compiles JVM/Native/SCRIPT, JS dies with `Internal compiler error: KofJS: unexpected op in switch case: KofConditionalJump[comparison=NE, operandType=int, trueLabel=3, falseLabel=4] [COMP002]`.
- **Bisect (measured):** `3d3261a6` = GREEN · **`09e40afb` = RED** (the #471/#473/#474 recovery). Not introduced by the docs→plataforma lane; recorded from a full-suite run on tip where my lane's own tests are green and this one fails at her commit too.
- **Hypothesis (recorded at filing — WRONG, kept for the record):** a `KofConditionalJump`-as-case-value colliding with tableswitch/lookupswitch operands in the emitter's case dispatch.
- **Root cause (measured, `a604798a`):** `09e40afb` (#471/#473/#474) changed the lowerer's numeric arms from `SUB + CJ(EQ)` to the canonical `KofBinary(EQ, switchType) + LOAD 0 + CJ(NE)` — the SAME shape the enum-identity and String (`kof_string_equals`) faces already emitted, and which `JsSwitchParser` already recognized for those two faces only. The primitive-`EQ` op fell into `isExpressionOp`, pushed a boolean onto the case stack, and the following `CJ(NE)` hit the parser's "unexpected op in switch case".
- **Fix (code, not the test — Q0):** `JsSwitchParser` learns the third canonical arm: primitive-`EQ` with stack `[subject, caseValue]` sets `primitiveEq`, skips the op (JS `switch` already compares by `===`) and the post-loop check accepts `CJ(NE)` alongside `stringEq`/`identityEq`. NaN never matches (`===` false = dcmpeq false parity, per the lowerer's own comment). No new backend branch, no silent fallback.
- **Proof:** `BackendParityTest` **19/19** (was the single tip failure; the fixture is the issue's own program, red before / green after) + full switch family green (6E-node environmental documented).
- **Closed by:** the plataforma-universal frente-total lane under the maintainer's 19/09 directive ("lane nao limita"); item was unclaimed for 3+ hours at tip-red.

- **Addendum (lane de issues, ship4 no tip `9711e940`):** o FIX acima fecha a face codegen (`BackendParityTest` 19/19) mas **`WorkflowE2ETest.retryFacesBothOutcomes` continua RED no tip** — o programa roda no JVM e produz `ok=flaky failed=boom skipped=...`, no JS o runner sai 0 com **stdout VAZIO** (face runtime da mesma água, não codegen de switch). Não é desta lane; rota `.18`. (`scheduleDelegatesToSchedulerAtAndFires` verde agora — coberto por `9711e940`.)
- **Addendum (plataforma-universal lane, 19/09 ~20:3x — causa medida):** o stdout vazio no JS é **INTERMITENTE** e o `.mjs` está CORRETO (contém os 4 `kofPrintln`); o mesmo binário roda 2/6 vezes com saída e 4/6 vazio, sempre `rc=0`. Repro isolado: compilar `retryFacesBothOutcomes` para JS e rodar o mesmo `Default.mjs` em laço — a perda correlaciona com o `time.sleep` do backoff `exponential(1,2)` dentro de `flow.run()` (retry). Não é codegen (o módulo está certo) nem desta lane; rota `.18`/JS-runtime: o runner fecha o `Context` antes de drenar a saída do caminho assíncrono. Pinned como flake conhecido, não mascarado.

## §345 — `println()` with zero arguments compiled clean and died at runtime with `NoSuchMethodError` — the builtin accepted any arity at the typer (#495) — ✅ FIXED 19/09 (`.22`; `SEM096` at compile time, all 4 targets — shared frontend)

- **Numbering note:** claimed as §343 in-flight; the docs lane published its own §343/§344 (JS-lane `09e40afb` faces) at the remote tip during my edit — per the §NNN shared-claim rule I renumber MY side (§345) and leave the remote sections untouched.
- **Symptom (issue #495):** `main() { println(); println("done") }` → clean build, then `java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: 'java.lang.Object Default.Main.println()'`. The body of #495 suggested emitting `System.out.println()` (blank line); the maintainer ruled in the thread (19/09): **"actually empty println should not compile"** — the fix is a diagnostic, not the suggested lowering.
- **Root cause (measured):** `BuiltinCallTyper` intercepts the receiverless `println`/`print` builtins (line ~126) and types VOID looping over **any** arity — including zero; `ExpressionPrintLowerer.lower` only handles `size() == 1` and returns -1 for 0 args, so the call fell through to the generic method-call emitter, which emitted `invokevirtual Default.Main.println()` — a method the class does not have. Silent at compile = R6 violation.
- **Fix (additive diagnostic, freeze-safe):** `BuiltinCallTyper` now reports `SEM096: println() needs an argument — println and print take the value to print (println(x)); for a blank line use println("")` when the builtin is called with zero args. Non-shadowing (same rule as `sleep`): if a user declaration named `println`/`print` resolves in scope, the builtin check is skipped and the user method keeps working. Script/JS/Native share the frontend — one diagnostic, honest on all 4 targets (parity rule 5).
- **Proof:** `PrintNoArgsE2ETest` (new, 5/5 green): issue verbatim → SEM096 names `println`; `print()` → SEM096; negative controls — `println("")` (the blank-line idiom the diagnostic points at), the 1-arg faces (`"oi"`, `42`, `3.5`, `true`) and a user `class Box` with `println(Int, Int)` all still compile. CLI repro on the rebuilt jar: `x.kf:3:5: error: ... [SEM096]` with correct file/line/column on build **and** `run`, on jvm/js/native; `kof run` (script) shows it too. Code reference uses the free `SEM096` (SEM094 reserved for the switch-return gate per DECISIONS §D-TROOL note, SEM095 taken by the same-name-builtin arity check at ExpressionTyper).

## §349 — JS `Set`/`List`/`Map` compared collection **elements** by identity (`kofValEq` had no Array/Set branch) — `setOf(listOf(1,2)).add(listOf(1,2))` returned `true` while the JVM deduplicated (#518) — ✅ FIXED 19/09 (`.15` issues lane; deep content compare, JVM oracle parity)

- **Numbering note:** claimed as §346 in-flight; the remote tip published §346–§348 (ship4) during the edit — per the §NNN shared-claim rule this side was renumbered §349 in the rebase; both sides preserved.
- **Symptom (issue #518, measured by reporter on 0.4.7-beta):** on JS, a Kof `List`/`Set` used as an element of another `Set` (and, same helper, as a `List` element or `Map` key) compared by identity: `add` said `true`, `contains` said `false`, `setOf(setOf(1)).size()` grew to 2. The JVM dedupes — `AbstractList.equals`/`AbstractSet.equals` compare content. Parity rule 5 violated silently.
- **Root cause (measured):** `kofValEq` (the shared JS helper behind `kofSetHas`, list `contains`/`indexOf` and map-key lookup) handled only three cases — identity, NaN, and objects with a synthetic `.equals` (records). A Kof `List` lowers to a plain JS `Array` and a `Set` to a plain JS `Set`; neither has `.equals`, so two equal-content collections fell through to `return false`. (The regression test for this was filed `@Disabled` by the #521 lane, which fixed the record half of the same helper.)
- **Fix (runtime-only, backward compatible):** `kofValEq` now recurses by content — `Array` vs `Array`: same length, element-by-element in order (`AbstractList.equals`); `Set` vs `Set`: same size, each element of one found in the other via `kofValEq` (never `Set.has` — SameValueZero on references is exactly the bug; `AbstractSet.equals`). Mixed kinds and non-collections keep the old paths untouched. The three equality helpers (`kofValEq`, `kofRecordEq`, `kofFpEq`) moved from `JsRuntimeCore` to a dedicated runtime slice `JsRuntimeEquality` (block `equality` in `JsRuntimeSlices`; core 579→540, under the locked baseline).
- **Proof:** `KofSetEqualityTest.collectionsAsElementsCompareByContentOnJs` — the verbatim issue repro pinned as golden (`false/true/false/false/1`), previously `@Disabled`, enabled; whole `KofSetEqualityTest` 21/21 green (includes #521's nested-record JVM+JS twins and every pre-existing list/map content test — no weak fallback); neighbors `NullableBoolTruthinessE2ETest` 15/15, `PrimitiveToStringCastE2ETest` 4/4, `NativeNullablePrimitiveContractE2ETest` 42 run / 0 fail / 14 skip (cross guards). Same helper serves `contains`/`indexOf`/map keys, so those faces are fixed transitively and guarded by the pre-existing content tests in the same file. Full-suite tally is NOT from this lane (maintainer directive 19/09: issues lane runs targeted tests only; reactor suite at pre-merge with `main` when the queue zeroes).
