## §351 — #518 landed with THREE gates red at the combined tip (registry byte-identity, §257 ConstantValue guard, JS size baseline): equality block registered 2x + `EQUALITY_RUNTIME` as `static final` + golden helper never learned the block — ✅ FIXED 19/09 (plataforma-universal frente total; raced with `e06c15a1`/`c59fb7aa`, resolved keep-both)

- **Symptom (measured 19/09, full suite on the tip after the ship4/#518 rebase):** 2533/3F — `JsRuntimeSliceRegistryTest.fullSelectionIsByteIdenticalToLegacyConcatenation`, `RuntimeConstantInliningGuardTest` (offender `JsRuntimeEquality.EQUALITY_RUNTIME=ConstantValue(literal)`), `ArtifactSizeTest.helloJsRuntimeSizeWithinBaseline` (`runtime JS inchou: 13975B > 13657B`).
- **Root cause (measured):** `8c3b7c9d` (#518) added `new Block("equality", ...)` to `JsRuntimeSlices.BLOCKS` **twice** (node then sees duplicated `kofValEq`/`kofRecordEq`/`kofFpEq` → `SyntaxError`), declared the field `static final String EQUALITY_RUNTIME = <text block>` — a compile-time `ConstantValue` that §257 forbids for runtime text consumed cross-class (house convention: `static String`, the other 23 slices have no `final`) — and never synced `legacyCoreRuntime()`, which mirrors the registry by hand.
- **The race (recorded honestly, policy "preserve both sides, redo yours on top"):** while this unit was in flight the issue lane landed the dedup (`e06c15a1`) and its own follow-up — the dedup's second `sed` had erased `ui-components`, and `c59fb7aa` restored it AND synced the golden. At the rebase both histories were kept: the remote's final registry/golden stand, and this commit's remaining root fix is the **`final` removal (§257)** + the position comment on the golden line. No line of the sibling's work was reverted; no assertion was loosened (Q5).
- **Proof:** the three gates green on the resolved tip in one run (`JsRuntimeSliceRegistryTest` 6/6, `RuntimeConstantInliningGuardTest` 2/2, `ArtifactSizeTest` 3-exec/3-skip-toolchain) + `BackendParityTest` 19/19 + full 4-module suite 2961 / **0F** / 27E=`node`-absent (host-ambiental; CI ubuntu runs them) — see fix commit.
- **Lesson (recorded for every lane):** touching `JsRuntimeSlices.BLOCKS` REQUIRES re-running the three guards (`RuntimeConstantInliningGuardTest`, `JsRuntimeSliceRegistryTest`, `ArtifactSizeTest`) in the same unit — not only the E2E of the face; they exist exactly to catch cross-class inlining and byte/size drift of a new runtime block.
- **Addendum (measured 19/09, tip `a84a191b` — recurrence, different file):** the SAME guard is red again, now on `JsRuntimeCollections.COLLECTIONS_RUNTIME=ConstantValue(literal)` landed by `6872bf79` (#386/#382 fatia 1). Root and remedy are identical to the §351 case above: a `static final String` runtime text is a javac compile-time constant that gets INLINED into cross-class consumers (stale-consumer false-green on incremental builds) — drop the `final` (house convention: `static String`, the other slices have no `final`). **NOT fixed here:** `JsRuntimeCollections.java` is the `#386` lane's file and carries an active claim; this entry records the red + the exact one-token remedy so the owner lane (or CI) closes it. Flagged in DOING by the X7-2 lane (19/09 ~21:2x) and re-measured by this lane on the maintainer's host.

## §352 — #386/#382 native gaps taken at compile time: Float×sort (NAT001) and Object-valued containsValue (NAT002) on the native targets — ✅ FIXED 21/09 (NAT001 + NAT002 CLOSED; both faces run in parity on the 3 native targets)

- **Symptom (measured 19/09):** `List<Float>.sort()` and `Map<_,Object>.containsValue(v)` on Native are rejected at compile with `NAT001`/`NAT002`; JVM/Script/JS run both normally (goldens in `CollectionMethodsStdlibE2ETest`, JS/Script parity green).
- **Root cause (why not silently "fixed"):** (a) Float sort — the riscv→aarch translator has no `flw` (32-bit FP load), so single-precision comparisons would need a widening dance the cross runtime does not have; a wrong order shipped silently violates freeze rule 5, so the pair (sort, Float, native) gets the honest diagnostic. **(a) RESOLVED 21/09 — see the NAT001 bullet below** (the "no `flw`" blocker held only for the load-mnemonic route; `fmv.w.x`+`fcvt.d.s` were already translatable). Double sort IS implemented (`flt.d`/`feq.d` + `ucomisd`, with `Double.compare` semantics measured on the JDK oracle: NaN largest, NaN==NaN, -0.0 < 0.0). (b) Object-valued `containsValue` — native `Map<_,Object>` slots mix MAGIC boxes (Int/Long, boxed per §284) with RAW bit patterns (Double: `put` into a declared-Object map is legal on the JVM oracle — measured `put 7` then `put 2.5` on the same map), and a raw bit pattern is indistinguishable from a box header without dereferencing it — which SIGSEGVs on the Double slot. Any static tag is wrong for a mixed map, so the whole (containsValue, Object-value, native) family refused with NAT002 instead of guessing. **(b) RESOLVED 21/09 — see the NAT002 bullet below.**
- **Catalogued (Q7):** the complete resolutions are (a) ✅ DONE 21/09 — the widening route (`cvtss2sd` / `fmv.w.x`+`fcvt.d.s`) needed no new translator mnemonic; `sortTag` gained 3 and `CollectionMethodGates.floatSortUnsupportedOnNative` + its NAT001 branch are GONE (see the bullet below); (b) ✅ DONE 21/09 — boxed storage for Object slots on native (the smallest form of the plan) + dynamic runtime classification; see the NAT002 bullet. Both live in `CollectionMethodGates` + one guard at each lower site — greppable by the code itself.
- **NAT001 FECHADO (21/09, lane nat — follow-up of §374-native):** Float sort runs on the 3 native targets with the SAME `Double.compare` semantics. The slot keeps the raw 32 bits (measured: `mov $0x3fc00000` for 1.5f), the runtime widens to double (`cvtss2sd` on x86_64; `fmv.w.x`+`fcvt.d.s` on the cross — all already known to the aarch64 translator) and reuses the measured double compare; new `sortTag` **3**. **Two pre-existing faces fixed along the way (Q4):** (i) the x86 `kof_list_cmp` ±0.0 tie-break tested bit 62 (`addq`) instead of the sign — now `testq`; (ii) the aarch64 translator did not map riscv `x0` (hardwired zero) to `xzr`, so `slt t2, a0, x0` translated to `cmp x0, x0` → always false — silently wrong for the Double path too. **Proof (Q0/Q1, same commit):** `CollectionMethodsStdlibE2ETest#floatSortRunsOnNativeWithDoubleCompareSemantics` — golden measured on the JVM oracle (order + ±0.0 for Float AND Double + NaN last) byte-identical on x86_64, riscv64 and aarch64 (qemu; honest skip without toolchain). Neighbors green: `NativeE2ETest` 67/67, `NativeRiscv64E2ETest`/`NativeAarch64E2ETest` 53 each (1 skip), `KofConcurrency2Test` 48/48.
- **NAT002 FECHADO (21/09, lane nat — follow-up of §374-native):** Object-valued `containsValue` runs on the 3 native targets in parity. **Design (after measurement):** the per-entry value-kind header in the map struct was measured and DROPPED — a static `Object` argument can physically be a box, a String or a raw pointer and cannot be classified at compile time; probing raw bits as a pointer SIGSEGVs. The shipped path is the smallest sound form of (b): (i) **storage normalization** — every primitive written into an Object-typed value slot is boxed (`kof_box_*`, the §284 boxes; new `CollectionCallLowerer.referenceSlotPrim` guards `put`/`getOrDefault`/`putIfAbsent`/`containsValue`); (ii) **dynamic runtime classification** — new `kof_value_kind` (x86_64 and riscv/aarch64) returns 0 raw/pointer, 1 String, 2 box, **guarded by the heap bounds** (`kof_heap_low`..`kof_heap_high` on x86; `_kof_heap`..`_kof_heap_end` on the cross arena) before ANY deref, so a raw bit pattern (Double/Float) is never dereferenced; (iii) `CollectionMethodGates.valueCmpTag` Object value → new tag **6 dynamic** (was −1/NAT002; the header attempt had made it 3/miss): `kof_map_contains_value` probes the arg once, probes each entry, and compares box/box (`kof_box_equals`) or str/str (`kof_string_equals`), ptr/ptr raw `cmpq`; family mismatch → miss. Static tags 0/1/2/3 unchanged. The NAT002 refusal and its guard are GONE.
- **NAT002 Q4 bonus (fixed in the same slice):** raw primitives in Object maps now PRINT correctly on native — `println(o.get("d"))` printed an empty line (box-to-string probe missing for raw slots), now prints `2.5`; same for Bool. **Found, NOT ours, catalogued as §432:** JVM `getOrDefault(k, <primitive>)` on an Object-valued map dies with `VerifyError` (emitter overwrites the slot V with the call-site arg type) — JVM codegen, out of this slice; the native side is correct.
- **NAT002 proof (Q0/Q1, same commit):** `CollectionMethodsStdlibE2ETest#objectValuedContainsValueRunsOnNativeInParity` — mixed `Map<String,Object>` (Double/Int/Bool + Double/String entering via Object-typed args), hits by value, family-mismatch misses, `-0.0 ≠ 0.0` (bit-a-bit) and boxed print; golden measured on the JVM oracle, byte-identical on x86_64, riscv64 and aarch64 (qemu; honest skip without toolchain). Neighbors green on the slice: `CollectionMethodsStdlibE2ETest` 11/11, `KofMapSetTest` 14, `MapGetOrDefaultTest` 5, `MapReturnElementTypeTest` 3, `BareCollectionFieldE2ETest` 8, `BareCollectionPrimitiveArgE2ETest` 12, `NativeE2ETest` 67, `KofConcurrency2Test` 48, `NativeRiscv64E2ETest`/`NativeAarch64E2ETest` 53 each (1 skip) = 263 tests, 0F.
- **Same-family pre-existing note (recorded, not ours):** Int-argument queries into Long collections (`List<Long>.contains(2)`/`indexOf(2)`) are `false` on the JVM (equals, measured -1) and raw-identity `true` on native — pre-§382 behavior of `contains` inherited by `indexOf`/`lastIndexOf`; resolution belongs to a boxed-slot plan (same (b) as above), not to this slice.
## §353 — a lambda whose body DIRECTLY returns an `io` method result is rejected with SEM014 (the typer does not resolve `kof.io` return types in that position) — ✅ FIXED 21/09 (compiler lane; pins `WorkflowE2ETest.lambdaBodyWithIoBoolCompilesAndRuns` 24/24 + `NullSafetyE2ETest` 14/14)

- **Numbering note:** claimed as §352 in-flight; the remote tip published §352 (#386/#382 native gaps, `f32094e8`) during this edit — per the §NNN shared-claim rule this side is renumbered §353; both sides preserved.

- **Symptom (measured 19/09):** with `import kof.workflow`, `job("e", () -> File("x").exists())` fails to compile: `:0:0: error: Argument 2 of 'job': expected 'function' but got 'function' [SEM014]`. The same for `Directory("x").exists()`, `File("x").isFile()`, `File("x").isDirectory()`, `File("x").writeText(...)`, `File(p).copyTo(q)`. It is not the `job` signature: the identical io call compiles and runs outside a lambda (`var b = File("x").exists(); println(b)` — green in `IoE2ETest`).
- **Not the same bug (control, all compile):** a lambda returning a `String`/`List` method result in the same position is fine — `() -> "x".startsWith("x")`, `() -> listOf(1,2).contains(1)`, `() -> "x".isEmpty()`, `() -> "x".length == 1`.
- **Root cause (measured 19/09, CONFIRMED 21/09):** `io` methods are resolved by the `KofIo` dispatcher (`KofIo.instanceMethod`/`staticMethod`) rather than by the general type checker; lambda return-type inference therefore sees an unresolved receiver and types the body as `Unknown`/Void, and the `() -> Bool` formal then rejects it. The asymmetry was exactly between the two typers: the EMIT typer (`MethodCallTyper`, `KofIo.isIoType` branch) knew kof.io all along — the SEMANTIC one (`SemMethodCallTyper.infer`, which types lambda bodies) had no io branch and fell to `UNKNOWN`.
- **Fix (additive, mirrors the emit table):** `SemMethodCallTyper.infer` gained the `KofIo.isIoType` branch (instance-method return via `KofIo.instanceMethod`, identity `path()` returns the receiver) — same dispatcher, same table, zero new contracts (programs that compiled still compile; only rejected programs are now accepted). Q0 proof: `WorkflowE2ETest#lambdaBodyWithIoBoolCompilesAndRuns` is RED (`expected 'function' but got 'function'`, stashed-fix run) / GREEN with the fix, JVM==JS byte-parity with real disk (`writeText` → `exists` true, missing file → job false).
- **Revealed by the fix (both landed here, same commit):** typing io correctly exposed unsound code the blind typer had swallowed. (a) `MakealivePrimitivesE2ETest.ioStateRoundTripRunsJvmJsNativeCompiles` dereferenced `readText()` (a `String?`) with NO guard — a real SEM049, fixed in the test by the documented idiom `back != null && back.length`. (b) `MakealiveFsProviderE2ETest.fsRead` uses the **early-return narrowing** shape `if (t == null) { return } ... t.split(...)` — SG-005 narrowing existed only inside branches, never AFTER a guaranteed-exit `if` without else. Completed it (additive): `StatementAnalyzer.IfStmt` now applies the else-side narrowing to the enclosing scope when the then-branch definitely exits (`thenBranchExits`: return/throw/continue/break/block-last/if-both); `NullSafetyE2ETest` 14/14 pins the positive (runs, correct output) AND the negative twin (no exit → SEM049 still fires — no false acceptance).
- **Workaround (idiom, still valid, kept in the example):** bind the io result to an explicit `Bool` before returning — `Bool ok = File(p).exists(); return ok`. `examples/ci/ci-pipeline.kf` keeps its form (backward compatible); the direct `() -> File(p).exists()` is now legal too.
- **Minimal repro:** `import kof.workflow` + `main() { var j = job("e", () -> File("x").exists()) }` — was SEM014, now compiles; the pre-fix jar reproduces the error (measured both sides in-session).
- **Found by:** `CmdWorkflowTest.realCiPipelineExampleRunsEndToEnd` (2.5 E2E) — the example carries the workaround + an inline note pointing here. **Edge hunt (21/09, Q4) surfaced §400** (named top-level function as a value → SEM011, pre-existing on 0.4.7, catalogued separately).

## §354 — inherited-field assignment lowered to an `Object` temporary (`Object var11 = w; this.width = var11;`, PUTFIELD descriptor `Ljava/lang/Object;` / owner `?` → `NoClassDefFoundError: "?"`) — the superclass name was not canonicalized end-to-end — ✅ FIXED 19/09 (3 faces, one family; pins `InheritedFieldAssignE2ETest` 9/9)

- **Symptom (measured on tip `128f409c`):** (a) `super.width = w` (Float field inherited from `Shape`) compiles silently, decompiles to `Object var11 = w; this.width = var11;` and dies at load with `NoClassDefFoundError: "?"` (receiver `super` typed UNKNOWN → spill `KofStoreLocal(UNKNOWN)` + `KofStoreField(owner "?")`). (b) cross-package `extends` with an EXPLICIT import (`import foo.bar.Shape`) → false SEM025 "Cannot resolve field 'width' on type 'Rect'"; bare `width = w` in the same class → false SEM011. (c) `extends` via wildcard (`import foo.bar.*`) compiles but emits raw `super_class "Shape"` → `NoClassDefFoundError: Shape` at load.
- **Root cause (one family — the SUPERCLASS NAME is not canonical):** `SymbolTableBuilder` stores `superClass()` qualified when an explicit import exists (`"foo.bar.Shape"`), RAW under wildcard (`"Shape"`), and the registry (`knownClasses`) is keyed by SIMPLE name. (a) nothing typed the `super` receiver — the READ path had the special case (`ExpressionLowerer:323-329`), the WRITE path and BOTH typers did not; (b) `MemberResolver`'s BFS enqueued the stored name without normalizing, so the chain broke at any dotted-stored super; (c) `CompilerClassLowering.lowerClass` emitted the stored name with dots→slashes only, never consulting the registry.
- **Fix (general, additive, no contract change):** single source in `HierarchyResolver` — `simpleOfStored`/`canonicalSuperInternal`/`superTypeOf` (registry-first, the same identity model as §308); `findSuperClass` registry-first; `MemberResolver` BFS normalizes super+interfaces (shared `enqueueAncestors`); the #360 `firstCommonAncestor` BFS normalized too; BOTH typers (`ExpressionTyper`, `SemExpressionTyper`) type the `super` receiver as the superclass class-type, so all existing resolution/diagnostic paths take over (e.g. `super.count = v` on a STATIC now emits a typed `putstatic` instead of invalid `putfield`); `CompilerClassLowering` emits the canonical internal name; the fallback receiver push keeps the real `this` type.
- **Proof (Q0 red-before/green-after):** faces (a)/(b)/(c) reproduced red on the pre-fix tip in the session harness (SEM025 / `NoClassDefFoundError: Shape` / `NoClassDefFoundError: "?"`); after the fix all green. Formal pins `InheritedFieldAssignE2ETest` 9/9 — super write + compound + two-level (grandparent field, `super.v` through Mid) + static-super `putstatic` guard + cross-package explicit/wildcard/bare + script parity — with javap assertions on the report's literal form: `Field Shape.width:F` and typed `fstore` (no `Object` temp for the value), and no `putfield ... Ljava/lang/Object` for inherited fields. Frozen semantics untouched (freeze rules 1/4/6): the fix RESTORES the documented expected behavior, changes no operator/precedence/null-flow contract.
- **Sister bug from the same report — "enum generated in the wrong package":** ALREADY FIXED on tip by §308/D-ENUM207 (#445, `c6e0b7db`); the observed symptom came from the STALE `lib/kof.jar` (built 19/09 ~17:39, pre-§308) that `bin/kof` executes — a tip-built `kof-cli` jar emits `foo/bar/Status.class` correctly (verified on the CLI layout of the issue). Placement is now pinned by `EnumPackagePlacementE2ETest` 7/7 (direct source, deep package, explicit import, same-package multi-file, two packages, root guard, script parity). Operational lesson: `lib/kof.jar` is NOT rebuilt by `mvn` — rebuild it (or stop trusting `bin/kof`) after any compiler fix, else the fix is invisible from the CLI.

## §355 — the erasure river, family 1: the type variable `T` reached the JVM emit sites as a phantom `ClassType("","T")` in NESTED positions and with the BOUND swallowed by the parser — ✅ FIXED 19/09 (#399 #363 #368 #375; `GenericErasureJvmE2ETest` 6/6)

- **Symptom (measured on tip `f32094e8`):** #399 `List<T>` field + `peek(): T` → `NoClassDefFoundError: T` (getfield `[List<T>.T;`-style phantom: checkcast/getter owner `T`); #363 `items[i]` element checkcast `T` → same crash; #368 `item.toString()` with `item: T` → `invokevirtual` owner `T`; #375 `<T : Animal>` — the parser swallowed the bound and registered TWO type-params (`["T","Animal"]`), so `item.name` was typed on the phantom `Animal`-as-typevar/Object and the erasure had nothing to erase to.
- **Root cause (one river, four beds):** `resolveWithTypeParams`/`MemberResolver.resolveType` matched the type-var name only at the TOP of the type; nested leaves (`List<T>`, `T[]`, nullable) stayed `ClassType("","T")`. The parser dropped bounds entirely; `Type.TypeVariable` had no `bound` field. Every emit site that trusts the symbol's Type (owner, descriptor, checkcast) faithfully printed the phantom.
- **Fix (central, additive):** parser records the bound INSIDE the entry (`"T: Animal"` — no AST-shape change, old readers unaffected); `TypeVariable(name, bound)`; new `TypeParams` is the single reader of raw entries (`name/boundText/names/contains/variable/symbol/rewrite`) and `rewrite` recurses args/components/nullable substituting scope type-params; `JvmTypeMapper.toDescriptor` erases `T`→bound (unbounded→Object, javac semantics); `JvmOpEmitter` resolves TypeVariable owners via `erasureInternalName`; member field/method access on a bounded receiver unwraps to the bound (typer + lowerer pairs). Untyped paths keep the exact old behavior (rewrite returns the same instance when no leaf matches).
- **Proof:** `GenericErasureJvmE2ETest` 6/6 (four issues verbatim + bounded method-call erasure + script non-regression). Script/JS/Native outputs unchanged where they worked (no descriptor on those paths) — BackendParityTest 19/19, all `Generic*` neighbors green (100/100 targeted run).
- **Numbering note:** claimed as §353 in-flight; the remote tip published §353 (lambda SEM014) and §354 (inherited-field assign) during this unit — renumbered to the next free §355 here per the shared-claim rule.
## §356 — the erasure river, family 2: generic INTERFACE methods lowered with `List.of()` type-params (descriptor `()LT;` literal → NoSuchMethodError) and the covariant-bridge generator only scanned the superclass and never boxed primitives or bridged erased PARAMETERS — ✅ FIXED 19/09 (#385 #366 #365; `GenericIfaceEmitE2ETest` 7/7)

- **Symptom:** #385 `printWrapped(w: Wrapper<String>) { w.get() }` → `NoSuchMethodError: Wrapper.get()Ljava/lang/Object;` — the emitted interface had `LT;` descriptors while call sites (semantic side, #160) correctly erased to Object. #366 same via an interface-typed var. #365 `IntHolder extends Holder<Int>`: bridge `(I)` vs parent `(Object)` — before, VerifyError `areturn` on `int` (bridge existed from #248 without box); and a VOID parent method with a type-var PARAM (`set(v: T)` implemented as `set(v: Int)`) got NO bridge at all → `AbstractMethodError` (found by the adversarial same-arity test, Q4).
- **Root cause:** `lowerInterface` discarded `iface.typeParameters()`; bridge generation keyed on name+arity against the SUPERCLASS only, with raw-type equality (missed `Int`×`T` and interface parents).
- **Fix:** interface type-params flow to `lowerMethod`/`lowerField`; bridges now scan parents AND interfaces, match by ERASURE key (new `erasureKey` — args nested with type-vars are bridged with unbox/checkcast at the boundary, primitives box on return), duplicate-slot guard by erasure (no ClassFormatError on overloads).
- **Proof:** `GenericIfaceEmitE2ETest` 7/7 (three issues + parent-var dispatch + iface-primitive bridge + same-arity-overload + script). Bytecode verified: `Wrapper.get()Ljava/lang/Object;`, `IntHolder.getValue()Ljava/lang/Object;` with `invokestatic Integer.valueOf`. (+ `check_500` kept green by extracting `lowerInterface`/`lowerRecord` to `CompilerIfaceRecordLowering` — the mother class would cross 600.)

## §357 — the erasure river, family 3: field `T[]` emitted descriptor `[LT;` (NoClassDefFoundError on `<init>` load), cast target `x as T[]` emitted `checkcast [LT;`, and the now-honest JVM type decision (primitive array into erased reference-array slot) needed a code — ✅ FIXED 19/09 (#295; SEM098; `GenericFieldArrayEraseE2ETest` 5/5)

- **Symptom:** #295 `class Stack<T> { T[] items }` + `s.items = new Int[10]` → NoClassDefFoundError/VerifyError at LOAD (field descriptor `[LT;` — the phantom component, same root as §355).
- **Fix:** component erasure comes free with §355 (rewrite recurses ArrayType). Cast/instanceof targets now flow through `driver.currentTypeParams` (set in `lowerMethod`/`lowerConstructor`, save/restore like `currentLoweringOwner`) so `new String[cap] as T[]` emits `checkcast [Ljava/lang/Object;`. The remaining `Int[] → T[]` assignment is NOT a bug: with the descriptor correct it is a genuine JVM type error (`int[]` is not a subtype of `Object[]`, JVMS 4.10.1 — javac rejects it identically), and boxing element-wise would create alias-divergent copies (silent, worse). It is now `SEM098` with the Kof-idiom hint (`List<Int>`), gated to `Target.JVM` and skipped under `driver.interpreting` — the interpreter lowers with `target = JVM` by convention (`prepareForInterpretation`), and rejecting a program that always ran on script would break freeze rule 2.
- **Proof:** 5/5 — positive `as T[]` run (pop order `b\na`), SEM098 on JVM, script still prints `ok`, `.class` contains `[Ljava/lang/Object;` and not `[LT;`, `instanceof` on bounded receiver.

## §358 — PRE-EXISTING native gap (surfaced while validating §355): `item.toString()` on an UNBOUNDED `T` receiver lowers to a bare `call toString` on the native targets → `ld: undefined reference to 'toString'` — ✅ FIXED 21/09 (`NAT004` honest refusal at compile; never the cryptic link-fail)

- **Symptom (measured 19/09):** `java -jar kof-cli ... run ~/med/g/i368/Main.kf --target native` → `ld failed: undefined reference to 'toString'` in `process`. #368 was filed against the JVM; its native twin fails the same way before and after the erasure river.
- **Root cause (observed):** `NativeBackend` emits the method name without a receiver-class mapping when the receiver's static type is a type variable erased to Object — there is no `kof_object_toString`-style dispatch wired for `toString()` on erased receivers.
- **Catalogued, not fixed here (Q7):** belongs to the native lane (same area as §352's NAT001/NAT002 honest-diagnostic pattern): either dynamic dispatch via the object header's toString slot or an honest `NAT00x` diagnostic at compile time — never the broken `call toString`. JVM/Script/JS are green for #368.
- **✅ FIXED 21/09 (nat orphan lane, owner 9093):** the refused route is the honest `NAT00x` face. Rationale measured: the cross vtable index of `toString` is **per class** (`NativeClassMeta.collectVirtualMethods` orders by the class hierarchy), and `Object`'s own methods are excluded from every vtable — so an erased `T` (→ `Object`) has **no static slot** to dispatch; and a primitive argument (`process(42)`) is passed as a **raw qword**, not a heap object. Dynamic dispatch is therefore not expressible; the fix is `ExpressionInstanceCallLowerer` refusing the call at lowering when the receiver is an unbounded `TypeVariable` on a native target: `'<m>' on an unbounded type parameter is not supported on the native target yet (NAT004) — give the type parameter an upper bound or use JVM/JS/Script`. This replaces the pre-fix `ld: undefined reference to 'toString'` (reproduced verbatim on the tip 21/09).
- **Q1 proof:** `NativeGenericDispatchGapE2ETest` **2/2** — `unboundedTypeParamMethodCallRefusedOnNative` (JVM keeps printing `42\nhello\n` byte-identical, the 3 native targets refuse with `NAT004`, no toolchain needed since the refusal is at lowering) + `boundedTypeParamStaysGreenOnNative` (control: `T : Animal` erases to the bound, **no** `NAT004`). Q3 matrix: happy path (JVM) + expected error (native NAT004) + bound edge. Neighbors green: `NativeE2ETest` 67/67, `NativeRiscv64E2ETest` 53, `NativeAarch64E2ETest` 53 (1 skip each), `NativeErasureBoxE2ETest` 6/6, `BareCollectionPrimitiveArgE2ETest` + `KofConcurrency2Test` + `Generic*` all green.
- **Residual (honest, NOT this fix):** the true `toString` on a **bounded**/concrete receiver still dispatches via the vtable (unchanged); a future real fix for the unbounded case would need a uniform `Object.toString` slot in every vtable (nat lane project, rule 6). `§352` (NAT001 Float-sort / NAT002 Object-valued containsValue) remains GAPS-OPEN, unaffected.
## §360 — `process.spawn` handle ops (`readLine`/`write`/`exitCode`/`kill`/`alive`) lowered to a raw `invokevirtual java/lang/Long.readLine` → `NoSuchMethodError` at RUNTIME on the JVM — the `isHandle` branch was DEAD CODE (dispatcher never routed a Long receiver to it) — ✅ FIXED 19/09 (found while landing the JS face of F10; pins `ProcessSpawnE2ETest` 4/4)

- **Numbering note:** claimed as §355 in-flight; the remote tip had ALREADY published §355 (erasure river family 1, `16f16081`) when this entry landed (4ed9bb2f shipped with stash-conflict markers too) — per the §NNN shared-claim rule renumbered to §360 by the cleanup commit; entry content untouched.
- **Symptom (measured 19/09):** `val h = process.spawn("echo", "vivo"); println(h.readLine())` compiles clean on the JVM (the SEM typer resolves handle ops via `KofProcess.handleMethod`) and dies at run: `java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: 'java.lang.String java.lang.Long.readLine()'`. Every handle op had the same leak; only the SPAWN call itself (a static `KofCall(FUNCTION)`) worked.
- **Root cause:** the emit branch for handle ops lives in `CollectionCallLowerer.lower` (checks `KofProcess.isHandle(recvType)`), but the dispatcher in `ExpressionInstanceCallLowerer` only consults that lowerer for **List/Channel/Map/Set** receivers — a `java.lang.Long` receiver fell through to generic virtual emission. The branch was NEVER reachable. Why the suite missed it for ~3 weeks: every existing F10 pin (`DomainGapCodesTest` JVM case, `WorkflowPrimitivesE2ETest`) only asserted COMPILATION or never touched a handle op at run — "compiles" was treated as "works" (Q1 violation the other direction: proof existed, but it proved less than the claim).
- **Fix (routing only, no contract change):** `ExpressionInstanceCallLowerer` now routes `KofProcess.isHandle(recvType)` into `CollectionCallLowerer.lower` (the branch was already written; it just needed a caller). Behavior emitted = the statics the descriptors already promised (`kof_spawn_read_line` etc.). No semantics frozen by the freeze moved: this surface had NO working behavior to preserve (any real program died at load), so the fix is strictly additive (freeze rule 2).
- **Proof:** new `ProcessSpawnE2ETest` 4/4 runs the handle ops on BOTH targets with byte-parity JVM==JS (echo `readLine`, EOF → `""`, failed spawn → honest dead handle `-1`, `exitCode` alive sentinel `Integer.MIN_VALUE`, `kill` → dead) — red before the routing fix (reproduced: the `NoSuchMethodError` above), green after. MEASURED quirk kept honest: the JVM binding redirects child stdin from `/dev/null`, so `write` is a no-op on both targets today — piping live input is a contract change (rule 6), not a parity bug; documented in the test's javadoc and the parity matrix.
- **Sister landing of the same unit:** the JS face of `process.spawn` (host binding `KofJsProcessBridge.processSpawn` + handle proxies, shims in `JsRuntimeIo`, routing `JsRuntimeProcessShellOps`, lowerer gate narrowed to Native-only, `DomainGapCodesTest.processSpawnOnJs` flipped from PROC001-pin to no-gap) — the plan clause "pipeline JS needs live-pipe spawn" is now measured as PARTIALLY satisfied: the binding exists; the public `write` face is `/dev/null`-gated (rule 6). The `JsRuntimeOps` growth that the split extracted sits at the 500-gate tolerance band (577→537 after `JsRuntimeProcessShellOps`).

## §359 — cross riscv64/aarch64 collection-method link was BROKEN at the tip: `kof_list_add_all` never ported and `kof_list_cmp` jumped to the x86-only `kof_string_compare_to` — ✅ FIXED 19/09 (measured on the maintainer's host, which HAS the cross toolchain + qemu; `f32094e8` was authored on a host without them, so its cross E2E skipped)

- **Numbering note:** claimed as §354 in-flight; the remote tip published its own §354 (inherited-field `Object` temporary, `128f409c`) during this edit — per the §NNN shared-claim rule this side is renumbered §355 (the commit subject was reworded to match); both sides preserved. SECOND collision on the rebase: the remote tip had by then published §355–§358 (erasure-river JVM, `16f16081`/`c8d55a10`/`0aa6a307`) — same rule, final number §359; no number reused.

- **Symptom (measured 19/09, tip `a84a191b`):** `NativeRiscv64E2ETest.riscv64CollectionMethodsStdlibGolden` and `NativeAarch64E2ETest.aarch64CollectionMethodsStdlibGolden` FAIL at link: `undefined reference to 'kof_list_add_all'` (in `Default_Main_main`) and `undefined reference to 'kof_string_compare_to'` (in `kof_list_cmp`). The JVM/Script/JS faces were green, so the regression was invisible on a host where `assumeToolchain()` skips the cross suites — the lane's own commit message says "Sem qemu/cross-as neste host: os dois E2E cross entram skip-honesto".
- **Root cause (two independent omissions in `NativeRiscvAsmLookups0`, the `#386/#382` fatia-2 riscv slice):** (a) `kof_list_add_all` — one of the 7 collection methods the slice claims to port — was simply never written in riscv, yet `CollectionCallLowerer` emits a direct `call kof_list_add_all` on every target; (b) `kof_list_cmp`'s String branch did `j kof_string_compare_to`, the x86 runtime name; the riscv runtime defines the same operation as `String_compareTo` (`NativeRiscvAsmRtB36`, mapped by `NativeRiscvCrossOps` for the Kof `String.compareTo` call) — the symbol existed, the slice just used the wrong name.
- **Fix (minimal, native lane):** `NativeRiscvAsmLookups0` — `.Llk_str: j String_compareTo` (a0=this, a1=other, same convention `kof_list_cmp` already sets up) + a riscv `kof_list_add_all(a0=dst, a1=src) -> 0/1` mirroring the x86 `RuntimeListLookups` (copy via `kof_list_add`; `mudou` = final size != initial). aarch64 inherits both via the line-by-line translator.
- **Proof (Q0):** RED on the tip (exact undefined refs above, measured before the edit) → GREEN after: `NativeRiscv64E2ETest` **49/49 (1 skip)** + `NativeAarch64E2ETest` **49/49 (1 skip)** run under qemu on this host; controls `NativeStringCompareCrossTest` 2/2, `NativeStringUtf16CrossTest` 4/4, `NativeErasureBoxE2ETest` 6/6, `ArtifactSizeTest` 6/6, `KofSupervisorE2ETest` 16/16. The golden is the JVM oracle in `CollectionMethodsStdlibE2ETest` (program exercises `b.addAll(l)` and `str.sort()`).
- **Lesson (recorded for every lane):** a native/runtime slice is only proven where the cross suites actually EXECUTE. A host without `binutils-*-linux-gnu` + `qemu-user` makes `assumeToolchain()` skip them and a broken cross link looks green — the honest alternative is to declare the cross face UNVERIFIED on that host (as the commit message did) instead of marking the slice done. CI's `Native cross` job installs the toolchain precisely to be the gate.

## §361 — the boxed-nullable FIELD-writer cluster (the un-mirrored twin of §295(b) for LOCALS): `b.n = <primitivo>` on an `Int?/Long?/Double?/Char?` field stores the RAW integer where the slot/`putfield` descriptor is the BOXED reference — JVM `VerifyError` at class load, Native x86 SIGSEGV (core dump), while Script/JS print the value — ✅ FIXED 20/09 (box-cluster FULL; face String-literal reclassificada e resolvida como SEM012 pelo §368) (Int?/Long?/Double?/static/compound/Troolean faces ✅ FIXED and RE-VERIFIED 4-targets on tip `e293c4a5`; th and the `Char?` WRITE face was reclassified to §368 (String-literal into any `Char` field = phantom-accept, now SEM012 nos 4 alvos; char-literal `'x'` fica na caixa verde do §361). #278 field-writer cluster FULL)

- **Symptom (measured 4 targets, tip6 jar `0aa6a307`, behavior == tip `4d3e67d3` — the delta since is test/docs-only, and `cd6e2089`/`4d3e67d3` guard corpus never touches field writes):** `class Box { Int? n }` + `main() { var b = Box(); b.n = 42; println(b.n) }` → **JVM: `VerifyError: Bad type on operand stack — Type integer (current frame, stack[0]) is not assignable to reference type` at `Default/Main.main @12: astore_3`** (class-load time, even under `-Xverify:all`); the `java -cp dir Default.Main` launcher HIDES it behind the JavaFX message (rule of 09/12 — reflective `Run` exposes the truth). **Native x86-64: builds and SEGFAULTS** (`timeout: o comando monitorado despejou núcleo`). **Script and JS: print `42`** — cross-target divergence, rule 5 + R6 violation. Same face for `Long?` (`b.n = 7`), `Double?` (`b.v = 2.5`), `Char?` (`b.c = "x"`) — all JVM VerifyError; the `+=`/`++` compound field paths share the writer and fail at the same store. READ of a never-written nullable field (`println(b.n)`) prints `null` and non-nullable Int field write/read (`42`) is fine — the bug is EXCLUSIVELY the field-WRITER with a boxed-nullable target.
- **Root cause (pointer, not an edit — cluster boundary, rule 2):** `ExpressionFieldAssignLowerer.java:71` (static) and `:252` (instance) gate the erasure-box emission on `driver.erasesToReference(fld.type())` — and `erasesToReference` (CompilerTypeSupport.java:89-92) covers only TypeVariable/ClassType/ArrayType/UnknownType, i.e. **FALSE for `NullableType(primitive)`** — the EXACT trap §295(b)/§294-2a documented for the LOCAL writers (`TypeMetrics.isNullablePrimitive` is the precise predicate; §295(b) fixed the local cluster and left this twin). The constructor face `Box(42)`/`C(1)` on a field-class is NOT nullable-specific (a plain `class C { Int n }` + `C(1)` dies with the same `NoSuchMethodError 'void C.<init>(int)'` — that belongs to the phantom-arity family, separate report).
- **Why the #278 guard missed it:** `NullablePrimitiveAtomicityGuardE2ETest` (`cd6e2089`/`4d3e67d3`, 5/5) inspects return descriptors, call-site, `== null`, locals and the observable corpus — **fields are not in its corpus**, while the issue itself lists "descritores de campo" in scope 1 and the D-NULL-INTENT invariant (`docs/development/DECISIONS.md:226`) names `slot ⇔ load/store` for ALL storage. Partial guard = §241 trap ("entrega parcial do tipo §241 nunca passa o gate").
- **Fix (landed 20/09):** box the RHS when `TypeMetrics.isNullablePrimitive(fld.type())` on both `ExpressionFieldAssignLowerer` gates (simple static + simple instance; compound `+=`/`++` already routed through the same `boxIntoSlot` shape), i.e. `emitWideningIfNeeded(valueType, inner)` + `emitErasureBox(inner)` — same as the §295(b) local fix. **REAL root cause had a second layer not in the pointer above:** the first fix attempt (gate added as `else if`) shipped RED 7/9 anyway because `TypeMetrics.isPrimitiveType` **unwraps** `NullableType` (`isPrimitiveType(Int?) == true`, TypeMetrics.java:18) — the pre-existing primitive→primitive widening branch therefore swallowed every `Int?` store before the new gate was ever reached. The gate chain must exclude nullable from the plain-widening branch (`&& !isNullablePrimitive(...)`), otherwise a correct predicate is dead code. Lesson for any `isPrimitiveType` consumer: it means "primitive or nullable-primitive" — use `isNullablePrimitive` to Distinguish, and never stack an `else if` behind it for a nullable face.
- **Proof (measured):** `NullablePrimitiveFieldWriterE2ETest` (9 cases — `Int?`/`Long?`/`Double?`/`Char?` simple + `+=`/`++` compound + static + the 2 controls `null`-read and plain-`Int` write): **RED 7/9** (VerifyError "Type integer not assignable to java/lang/Integer", identical to the repro above) before the fix → **9/9 green** after; canaries `NullablePrimitiveAtomicityGuardE2ETest` (5/5) + `NullableBoolTruthinessE2ETest` unchanged (rule 1 — the widening exclusion keeps Script/JS byte-identical: `needsErasureBoxing` false there, box branch never fires). ASM face of the store site (Integer.valueOf at the `putfield`) is the guard-scope-4 extension.

**§361 addendum — face `Char?` RE-MEDIDA no tip do fix `e293c4a5` (docs lane, jar reconstruido; JVM via `Run` reflexivo `-Xverify:all`):** `class C { Char? c }` + `c.c = "x"` → **JVM ainda `VerifyError: Bad type on operand stack` @15 `putfield` (`Type 'java/lang/String' is not assignable to 'java/lang/Character'`)** — o box novo emite o String CRU no slot boxado de Character (falta o desvio char: unbox `String→char` ANTES do `Character.valueOf`; a maquinaaria ja existe no writer nao-nullable, nao espelhada no branch nullable); **Script morre na MESMA carga de classe** (launcher mascara atras da mensagem JavaFX — regra 12/09); **Native x86 builda e morre em EXECUCAO**: `type error: class java.lang.Integer cannot be cast to the boxed value` na LEITURA apos escrita char (box char como Integer no runtime nativo, cast de leitura espera Character — face distinta da JVM, mesma causa familia §295); **JS esta GREEN (`y`)** e as faces `Int?/Long?/Double?/Troolean/static/+=` foram RE-MEDIDAS VERDES nos 4 alvos — por isso PARTIAL e nao reopen total. Prova devida para a char face: RED no par `c.c = "x"` + `println(c.c)` nos 4 alvos no `NullablePrimitiveFieldWriterE2ETest` (o teste atual NAO cobre char-write com literal String no JVM — a causa do falso 9/9 para esta face). **RESOLVIDA 20/09 (reclassificada p/ §368):** a "maquinaria String->char do writer plain" provada INEXISTENTE (plain `Char c` + "x" tambem morria na carga — sonda `Runner` pre-gate); a resolucao honesta NAO e coercion (os LOCAIS rejeitam a forma — SEM021/SEM012, D-NOT-JAVA #484 recusou promotion String->char) — e o gate de atributibilidade do campo do §368, que agora da SEM012 identico nos 4 alvos. `Char?` com CHAR-literal `'x'` continua a caixa verde do §361 (matrix 4-alvos). §361 fecha como FULL.

## §362 — calls to a constructor that DOES NOT EXIST are SILENTLY ACCEPTED at compile time: `record P(Int x)` + `P(1,2)` → JVM `NoSuchMethodError 'void P.<init>(int,int)'` at RUNTIME while **Script prints `0` and JS prints `1`** (phantom object with default values, different numbers!); `class C { Int n }` + `C(1)`/`C("s")` → same silent accept, Native `ld` fails with `undefined reference to 'C_init_1'` — ✅ FIXED 20/09 (`BuiltinCallTyper.reportNoCtorArity` gate; measured on tip `4d3e67d3`; routed to the `.22` diagnostic family #469/#470; tracked as **#545**)

- **Symptom (matrix, tip6 jar `0aa6a307` == tip behavior):** `kof check` prints "no errors" for all repros. JVM builds fine and dies at RUNTIME: `P(1, 2)` → `NoSuchMethodError: 'void P.<init>(int, int)'`; `class C { Int n }` + `C(1)` → `'void C.<init>(int)'`; `C("s")` → `'void C.<init>(java.lang.String)'` (the type of the argument is never checked either). **Script: prints `0`. JS: prints `1`** for `P(1,2)` — the two interpreters silently CONSTRUCT a phantom object with defaults, and disagree with EACH OTHER on the value (rule 5 + R6: the worst class, no diagnostic anywhere in the chain). Native x86: `ld failed: undefined reference to 'C_init_1'` (the call site asks a constructor nobody emitted — an honest-ish link error but with a cryptic diagnostic, not a gap code).
- **Why it is a bug, not rule 6:** the corpus is explicit — records own the declared-arity canonical constructor, mutable classes own `constructor(...)` (AGENTS.md idiom table; `class X(...)` at the declaration is what records). Calling an undeclared shape must fail at COMPILE like #469/#470 established (SEM diagnostics for phantom record mutation/extends); emitting the call anyway = silent codegen loss, the exact #459 worst-class pattern.
- **Root pointer (no edit — `.22` diagnostic cluster):** the constructor resolution in the typer/`MemberResolver` path never validates the call shape against the class's REAL constructor set (records: arity only vs canonical; classes: declared `constructor(...)` or none), then every backend emits what it got: JVM `new+invokespecial` to a descriptor nobody lowers (ClassBuilder lowers only declared/implicit-no-arg/canonical); Script/JS build the object with default fields dropping the args entirely.
- **Fix face (owner):** a SEM diagnostic at the call site when no constructor matches (arity + type via the existing `satisfiesAbstract`-style tag machinery of §242); the canonical/record/ctor-declared shapes keep compiling byte-identical (freeze 1). Proof owed: RED matrix from this repro (check now says "no errors"), GREEN with the SEM code, `CodegenKitchenSinkTest`-style no phantom `<init>` descriptors survive at the emit boundary (the same "bytecode-honesty" net §305 used).
- **Related:** §361 (field-writer box — adjacent in the ctor/field cluster, different root); #469/#470 (same "phantom accepted at compile" family); #459 (silent codegen loss precedent).

- **Fix (landed 20/09, `57a0d5f0`):** the implicit `Class(args)`-without-`new` resolution in `BuiltinCallTyper` had the #323 type-check but a **null-arity silent fallthrough** — now an `else` calls `reportNoCtorArity`: SAME SEM023 + SAME exceptions as the `new` path (`SemExpressionTyper:262-273`); fires only when the class DECLARES constructors (arity mismatch); `class Z {}` + `Z()` (implicit default) stays legal, overload-by-arity untouched. **Proof (measured):** `ConstructorPhantomE2ETest` 7/7 — `P(1,2)`/`C(1,2)`/`C()` rejected on JVM+JS+Script (shared frontend — the `P[x=null]`/`1` phantom divergence is gone) with `no constructor of 'P' with 2 argument(s) (expected 1)`; controls green; `C("s")`-on-`ctor(Int)` was already SEM014 (#323). Neighbor battery 125 tests / 0 failures incl. StdlibIdiomsCompile 20/20 (rule 1).
## §363 — issue #464 ("Native AArch64: Float compound assignment (`+=`) yields NaN"): the root cause landed with §342 (`f9119550`, 19/09) but the issue stayed OPEN with zero isolation pin — the bare-`Float` compound matrix (`+= -= *= /=`, nullable twin, loop, register pressure) is now measured GREEN on all 4 targets at tip `1080238f` — ✅ CLOSED WITH PROOF 20/09 (cross-runtime lane; `FloatCompoundAssignE2ETest` + aarch/riscv mirrors)

- **Symptom (issue's claim):** `main() { Float x = 2.5; x += 1.0; println(x) }` → aarch64 `NaN` (JVM/x86_64/riscv64 `3.5`); the isolation table shows ONLY single-precision compound-assign broken. Note for re-verifiers: the issue's command `--target native --arch aarch64` does NOT exist in this CLI (measured: `build: unknown or incomplete flag: --arch`) — the effective target is `native.arm` / `Target.NATIVE_AARCH64`.
- **Measured at tip (`1080238f`, jar rebuilt from the same tree, qemu + sysroot host):** the verbatim repro prints `3.5` and EVERY row of the issue's isolation table plus all Q3 edges prints the oracle — the bug is already fixed. The root cause was exactly §342's: `NativeAarch64Translator`'s `fadd./fsub./fmul./fdiv.` block compared `mn.substring(5)` against `".s"` (always false), so every `.s` op emitted `d` registers and the `fmov w9, s0` read-back grabbed the low half of the double → `NaN`. `+=` has no special lowering — it is a `KofBinary(ADD)` on a float32 slot emitted as `fadd.s` (`NativeRiscvCrossOps.java:55`) and translated, so the one §342 line covers all compound float ops.
- **Q0 red-before proof (measured 20/09):** with the §342 line TEMPORARILY reverted (`substring(4)`→`substring(5)`) the new `aarch64FloatCompoundAssignIsolation` goes RED on the very first line (`expected <3.5…> but was <NaN…>` across the matrix) while the riscv mirror stays GREEN; restoring makes the matrix green. No re-landing of the fix — it is in the tip; what was missing was the pin.
- **Proof (this unit):** shared golden `FloatCompoundAssignE2ETest` 2/2 (JVM MEDIDO `3.5/3.5/5.0/2.5/3.75/6.0/2.0/4.0/3.5/6.0/1.0/10.5` + x86 parity) + `NativeAarch64E2ETest#aarch64FloatCompoundAssignIsolation` + `NativeRiscv64E2ETest#riscv64FloatCompoundAssignIsolation` (parity lock — riscv was never red, the mirror passes by construction). Isolation vs §342's mixed program: every compound operator on its OWN bare-`Float` local, bare `Float?` twin (nu, 3× sequential, inside a loop), Float-local += Float-local (register pressure), Double×Float mix. NEXT STEP (quem der o push): `gh issue close 464` apontando este § e o `f9119550`.
- **Related:** §342 (raiz — este pin fechava a issue na hora), §129 (unid. que expôs a face), bug 80 (irmão do tradutor), #259/N2 (o `+=` do `Float?` que chegou primeiro).

## §364 — the §359 cross collection-link fix (riscv `kof_list_add_all` port + `kof_list_cmp` redirect to `String_compareTo`) landed with ZERO edge coverage (golden só toca addAll-em-dst-vazio e sort de strings distintas) — plus a MEASURED hazard for the next agent: a fall-through label-alias for `kof_string_compare_to` passes `ld` and dies at runtime under `--gc-sections` — ✅ PINNED 20/09 (cross-runtime lane; `CrossRuntimePortsE2ETest` + aarch/riscv consumers)

- **Symptom (coverage gap, measured):** after §359 the goldens are green, but three contracts are unpinned: (a) addAll num dst JÁ populado (crescimento + o branch `mudou`=true com dst não-vazio), (b) addAll de src vazio em dst populado (false invariante, sem mutação), (c) `String_compareTo` ALCANÇADO POR `kof_list_cmp` (tail `j`) nos casos PREFIXO ("app" < "apple" — a contagem de units do contrato JVM, não byte-offset) e IGUAL (duas "apple" → cmp 0, o selection-sort mantém ambas). O `NativeStringCompareCrossTest` (§97) trava a forma-MÉTODO `.compareTo` — a entrada via sort é outro caminho de simbologia.
- **Fix (testes; o port em si é §359):** shared golden novo `CrossRuntimePortsE2ETest` (JVM+x86, MEDIDO 20/09: `true 5 false 1 app apple apple fig pear 1 2`) + `aarch64CrossRuntimePortsEdges` + `riscv64CrossRuntimePortsEdges`. Sensibilidade Q0 medida: com o redirect da §359 stubado (`li a0,0; ret`) os DOIS testes de aresta ficam RED nos DOIS archs (sort clobbered deixa "pear" primeiro) e o resto da vizinhança permanece verde.
- **Hazard registrado (medido nesta unidade, no tip pré-rebase `4ed9bb2f`):** a forma x86 (free function + stub do método chamando-a) foi tentada como alias de label fall-through no riscv (`.globl kof_string_compare_to` + `kof_string_compare_to:` antes de `String_compareTo:`): LINKA, mas o binário morre em `str.sort()` com "Runtime error: out of memory" em riscv64 E aarch64 (`nm`: o alias resolve no endereço do `kof_alloc`). Causa: `NativeArchEmitter.sectionizeTextFunctions` dá a CADA par `.globl`+label a própria `.section .text.<nome>,"ax"`, e o `ld --gc-sections` coletou a seção do corpo real (ninguém referenciava `String_compareTo` no programa) deixando o alias uma seção VAZIA → `j` para o lixo. Um stub `j String_compareTo` (reloc explícita) resolve; a escolha da §359 (redirecionar o call-site, menos um símbolo) é MAIS SIMPLES (regra 11) e foi a mantida. LIÇÃO: no runtime cross riscv/aarch NUNCA definir dois nomes para a mesma rotina via fall-through de label — seção vazia + gc-sections é o modo silencioso de quebrar.
- **Proof:** `CrossRuntimePortsE2ETest` 2/2 + consumidores green sob qemu (aarch 51/0F/1-skip, riscv 51/0F/1-skip — os 2 skips são o pin opt-in `KOF_ASM_GATE` das duas classes, DECISIONS 14/09); vizinhança: `NativeRiscvRuntimeSliceRegistryTest` 8/8 (byte-identity/providerIndex/needs fechados com o texto da §359), `CollectionMethodsStdlibE2ETest` 11/11, `NativeE2ETest` 66/66, `NativeStringCompareCrossTest` 2/2; battery total da unidade 193/0F/0E/2-skip.
- **Related:** §359 (o port pinado aqui), §97 (peça B36, dona de `String_compareTo`), §358 (conferido: NÃO tocado — compare_to recebe `String*` reais da List, nunca receiver `T` apagado), #382/#386 (família).

## §365 — a LEITURA de campo nullable-primitivo NUNCA-ESCRITO imprime `0` no JS enquanto JVM/Script/Native imprimem `null` (`class P { Int? n }` + `println(p.n)`): a invariante D-NULL-INTENT `slot ⇔ load/store` nao vale para o default de campo no backend JS — ✅ FIXED 20/09 (fix landado nas duas faces JS+SCRIPT; matriz 4-alvos do §361 fecha a leitura nunca-escrita do cluster #278) — **re-verified independently by the docs lane on tip `7a543b4f` (rebuilt jar): JS and Script print `null`; §361 matrix (Int/Long/Double/Troolean/static/compound) stays green 4-targets; `Char?` write REMAINS broken — root now named by §368 (the field-assignment typer gate), NOT the §361 box gate**

- **Symptom (measured 4 targets, jars `0aa6a307` E `e293c4a5` — comportamento IDENTICO nos dois tips, nao e do fix do §361):** `class P { Int? n }` + `main() { var p = P(); println(p.n) }` → JVM `null`, Script `null`, Native x86 `null` (rc=0), **JS `0`** — cross-target divergence (rule 5) + silent wrong value (R6). The never-written nullable field in JS carries the raw 0 default of the numeric slot instead of the boxed-null sentinel that the §295/§278 corpus defines for the other three targets; the D-NULL-INTENT invariant (`DECISIONS.md`, `slot ⇔ load/store`) is therefore NOT established for the JS *initialization* of boxed-nullable fields.
- **Root pointer (no edit — cluster `.22`):** JS backend field emission gives nullable-primitive fields the primitive default (`0`) instead of `null` at object construction (the constructor face of the same box-nullable family §361 fixed for stores; the *default-value* site was never in scope of #278 nor of the §361 fix).
- **Fix (landed 20/09):** TWO roots, not one — the pointer above (JS) was half the story. (1) `JsTypeMapper.defaultForType`: added `if (type instanceof Type.NullableType) return JsNull.KOF_NULL;` **before** the `isPrimitiveType` dispatch — `JsClassEmitter.insertFieldDefaults` passes the declared slot type verbatim, and `isPrimitiveType` **unwraps** `NullableType` (`TypeMetrics.java:18`, the same trap as §361) mapping `Int?`→`0`. (2) `KofInterpreterMembers.defaultValue`: added `if (t instanceof Type.NullableType) return null;` — the Script interpreter's absent-field read routed `Int?` through `JvmOpCollections.isPrimitiveType` → `0` as well; the measured matrix 361b caught SCRIPT red (`expected <null> but was <0>`), which this section's symptom line (written from the JS jar only) did NOT predict. Collection/`??`/map-miss `isPrimitive` sites untouched (§127 semantics preserved — they operate on non-nullable T).
- **Proof (measured):** `controlNeverWrittenNullableFieldReadsNull` in `NullablePrimitiveFieldWriterE2ETest` — **RED on SCRIPT** (`expected <null> but was <0>`, matrix 361b) and the JS face per the symptom → **9/9 green on all 4 targets** (JVM/Script/JS/Native-x86, matrix 361c BUILD SUCCESS) after both guards; neighbors unchanged: `NullablePrimitiveContractE2ETest` 26/26, `JsNullablePrimitiveIfIceTest` 4/4, `NullableBoolTruthinessE2ETest` 15/15 — freeze 1 kept (goldens `Bool n`→false, `Int n`→0 intact; §294-2a/§279 faces green). Related: §361 (writer faces — now PARTIAL; char face reclassified to §368), §295/§278 (box-nullable family), #278.

## §366 — Script perde o stdout de `process.run` em silencio: `process.run("echo", "x")` → JVM compilado imprime `x` (exit 0), o MESMO programa via `kof run` (interpreter) imprime linha VAZIA + `0` — divergence rule 5 + valor errado sem diagnostico (R6) — ✅ CLOSED 20/09 (nao-reproduzivel no tip; medido no jar do tip `e293c4a5` na abertura)
- **Status:** ✅ CLOSED 20/09 — **nao-reproduzivel no tip atual**: o MESMO reprodutor (fonte verbatim `var r = process.run("echo","x"); println(r.stdout); println(r.exitCode)` via `driver.interpret`) roda no interprete do tip `3be16f88` SEM o diff do §367 e da `x` / `0` identicos ao JVM (captura: surefire do `ProcessResultContentE2ETest` no tip SEM o fix do §367 — linha `F:0|x` VERDE nos dois alvos; o unico RED residuo era a impressao por identidade, que e o §367 e nao o §366). O stdout perdido medido em `e293c4a5` morreu em algum pouso do cluster interpreter/runtime entre 19 e 20/09 sem entrada propria — a paridade pedida como prova de fecho ("mesma fonte, mesma saida byte-a-byte") passa a ser fixada como teste PERMANENTE no mesmo commit do §367: `ProcessResultContentE2ETest.scriptPrintsProcessResultByContent` + `shellRunWithPrintsProcessResultByContent` (conteudo + campos, JVM x Script byte-a-byte). #547 fecha com esta evidencia; se re-aparecer, reabre como bug novo com repro.

- **Sintoma (matriz medida):** fonte `main() { var r = process.run("echo", "x"); println(r.stdout); println(r.exitCode) }` → **JVM (compilado, `Run` reflexivo): `x` / `0`**; **Script (`kof run`): `` / `0`** — stdout VAZIO, exitCode OK; **Native x86:** `PROC001` em tempo de compilacao (honesto — nao conta); **JS:** `run` = host `KofJsRunner` (E2E 15/15 byte-parity — nao reproduzido aqui) / node puro = diagnostico honesto ja catalogado. Um un-`assume` environmental: nenhum — o repro e deterministico nos dois alvos executaveis.
- **Ponteiro de raiz (sem edit — fronteira de cluster, regra 2):** o caminho do interpreter para `process.run` varargs nao propaga o stdout do `Result` real (ou monta um `Result` com `stdout=""`); como `exitCode` chega correto, a perda e seletiva no campo de saida — mesma vizinhanca que a `.22` esta editando agora (`KofInterpreterMembers.java` M na arvore real).
- **Face do fix (dono):** o run-path do interpreter devolve o mesmo `Result` do caminho compilado; prova devida: teste de paridade JVM×Script no `ProcessRunE2ETest`-estilo (mesma fonte, mesma saida byte-a-byte, §239) — RED neste repro antes, GREEN depois.

## §367 — `println(result)` de um `Result` de process/shell VAZA identidade Java em JVM e Script: `dev.kof.runtime.KofRuntime$ProcessResult@6f79caec` — `Kof nao e Java` (regra 8) + o golden do corpus para impressao de valor e por CONTEUDO (`record` → `P[x=1, y=2]`; training stdlib: "Result e o MESMO tipo — uma forma, nunca fork") — ✅ FIXED 20/09 (medido no jar do tip `e293c4a5`, JVM compilado + `kof run`; ancorado na **#548**)
- **Status:** ✅ FIXED 20/09 — printer de conteudo nos tres caminhos alcancaveis: `JvmRuntimeCore` (o `ProcessResult` do runtime ganha `toString()` estavel `ProcessResult[exitCode=..., stdout=..., stderr=...]` com newline de fim-truncado como no bridge JS), `KofInterpreterObjects` (o interpreter passa a imprimir o Objeto Result pelo MESMO conteudo — branch reflexivo, sem tocar em nenhum outro println: freeze 1) e `JsRuntimeIo`+`KofJsProcessBridge`+`KofJsRunner` (o host JS, que ja imprimia por conteudo, ganha o formato unificado da familia e para de depender do `Object.toString()` do proxy). RED 4/4 no tip limpo (medido com o fix stashado: JVM `@2d6d8735`, Script `@7169d668`, JS-host e shell-script idem) → GREEN 4/4 apos, `ProcessResultContentE2ETest` 4/4 (JVM + Script + JS-host + `shell.run` Script) — o par JVM×Script×JS e byte-a-byte e o hash sumiu da superficie; `ProcessSpawnE2ETest` 4/4 + `ShellE2ETest` 16/16 vizinhos verdes no mesmo surefire. Native: sem-face (o alvo recusa `process.run` com o gap honesto PROC001, nao alcancado por este caminho). #548 fecha com esta evidencia (CI do SHA empurrado e a prova final dos 4-alvos).

- **Sintoma (medido):** `main() { var r = process.run("echo", "x"); println(r) }` → JVM: `dev.kof.runtime.KofRuntime$ProcessResult@2d6d8735` (FQCN Java + identity hash na superficie do usuario, hash DIFERENTE a cada execucao = nondeterminismo visivel tambem); Script: mesmo vazamento; Native/JS: nao alcancaveis por este caminho (run = PROC001 / host runner nao media aqui). O `@`-toString e o `Object.toString()` cru — nenhum printer Kof foi invocado.
- **Por que e bug, nao regra 6:** o corpus define impressao por conteudo para dados (linhas de registro na matriz de conformancia; `Result` documentado como um tipo de forma unica da familia process/shell); vazar FQCN+hash de uma classe `dev.kof.runtime.*` e quebra de filosofia E do golden de conteudo — nao e escolha de design em aberto.
- **Face do fix (dona):** um printer de conteudo para os tipos `Result` do runtime (formato estavel tipo `ProcessResult[exitCode=0, stdout=..., stderr=...]`), nos dois caminhos (JVM emit + interpreter), com a matriz de paridade 4-alvos como prova; nenhum outro println muda (freeze 1).

Os LOCAIS das mesmas formas: `Char v = "x"` → **SEM021**; `v = "x"` (reassign) → **SEM012**; coleções: `l.add("x")` em `List<Int>` → **SEM056**. ## §369 — #431: the `extern` scalar ABI bound ONLY on JVM/JS — all three Native targets (x86-64/riscv64/aarch64) refused `FFI001` since §61; binding them exposed two real exit-path bugs (C stdio lost under the raw `_start`; aarch64 `exit(93)` hangs any process with live threads) — ✅ FIXED 20/09 (fatia 1 `6794ca21` x86-64 + fatia 2 `cc12f4d0` cross, gate+shim+E2E qemu no mesmo commit)

- **Symptom (measured):** issue #431 — `extern "libraylib.so" InitWindow(Int w, Int h, String title)` on `--target native` refused with `FFI001` although the JVM ran the same signature; §61 kept the gap open because dlopen from the raw `_start` segfaults on the maintainer's host. A raylib window cannot be opened from a Kof binary without a hand-written C wrapper — the iron rule 2 ("complexity belongs to the platform") was being violated by our own gap.
- **Root mechanism (fixed, landed):** the §61-recorded escape route — **no dlopen; direct link + `call sym@PLT`** — is the proven DB001/SQLite path (`-l:libsqlite3.so.0`, bare `call sqlite3_*` works from the raw `_start`). `CompilerPipeline.isExternBound` now opens for `target.isNative()` restricted to the scalar set with `library()` present (callbacks/struct/array/no-library keep `FFI001` AT THE DECL LINE, §350); the lowerer emits a raw-args `KofCall` owner `kof.ffi` + `"lib::symbol"`; `NativeFfiCall.emitX86/emitRiscv` marshal per-class SysV/LP64/AAPCS64 (int-class regs, float-class regs, ≥9 same-class args spill to the callee block), String↔`char*` = the UTF-8 payload at offset 24 (NULL→NULL), String return = boundary copy (`kof_ffi_from_cstr`, C buffer never freed — same contract as the JVM `strstr`); call-site arity/type validation SEM013/SEM014 (before: `abs(1,2,3)` compiled on the JVM and SIGSEGV'd at runtime; would have corrupted the native stack). ABI facts **measured under qemu** (golden = real measurement, never memory): the Debian riscv64 glibc passes AND returns FP in `fa0..fa7` (physical f10-f17) — not `ft0` (the `exp` disassembly ends its result chain in fa0; the cross runtime's own `strtod` already read fa0); the aarch64 emitter inherits the riscv text via the translator's `fa0→f0→d0` normalization, which IS the AAPCS64 register — one shim, both archs. `and sp, sp, X` is invalid in the aarch64 GAS (logicals reject SP as Rn) → align via `t3`. Cross link: `library()` resolves through the sysroot by **basename** (`-l:libc.so.6`/`-l:libm.so.6` or bare `-l<name>`); an absolute HOST path is wrong-arch there (documented in `training/idioms/interop.md`).
- **Bug 1 (found with proof, fixed):** C stdio output vanished — `extern puts(String)` returned `10` (the libc really ran) but the line never appeared: full-buffered pipe + raw `exit_group` has no `atexit`. Fix: `call fflush` before the exit in `_start` on ALL THREE native targets — x86 needs `%rdi=0` AND stack re-alignment (RED measured: first attempt segfaulted 139 with garbage RDI/misaligned rsp; GREEN with the `movq %rsp,%rbx; andq $-16` guard, the same idiom as the `pow` shim).
- **Bug 2 (found with proof, fixed):** the aarch64 `_start` exited with `exit(93)` (thread-only) while x86/riscv use `exit_group` (M32.3) — any live thread (`time.interval` scheduler, or a C library's internals like GLFW/raylib) kept the process alive FOREVER. RED measured: `aarch64ExitGroupKillsScheduler` times out at 20s with 93; GREEN in <1s with 94. Without this, every raylib-style program on aarch64 would hang at exit.
- **Proof (measured, same commits — Q0/Q1):** fatia 1 `FfiNativeE2ETest` **16/16**: InitWindow shape `void(Int,Int,String)` golden `InitWindow 800 450 [direct Kof FFI] first=100 len=14`, explicit `: void`, 0-arg, 4-arg, **9-arg spill**, mixed int/double per-class, `Float`/`Bool`, String-in + `String` return `"hello-c"`, back-compat `abs/atoi/sqrt/srand` with **JVM byte-parity** (regra 5), gaps: `Int[]`→FFI001 line=1, callback→FFI001, no-library→FFI001, SEM013/SEM014 at the CALL. Fatia 2 `FfiNativeCrossE2ETest` **6/6**: golden **byte-identical riscv64×aarch64** under qemu (`abs(-42)/abs(7)/strlen("")/puts=10/ldexp(2.0,3)=16.0 mixed-class/getenv String-return/getpid>0`), FFI001 array at the decl line, exit-group×2. Neighbors 629/0F/0E/2-skip (`Ffi*,*Extern*,NativeE2E,Native*E2E,BackendParity,DomainGapCodes,CompilerDriver,Lambda,Concurrency`); `check_500` sem crítico; Q2 green.
- **Still open (honest, this § does not cover):** struct/array/out-buffer ABI (D6) on Native (the JVM face landed in 3.8b, below), callback/upcall on Native (no mechanism — `FFI001` kept); riscv/aarch **≥9-arg spill and Float/Bool edges have no golden** — no cross C compiler exists on the host to build a fixture and libc has no 9-arg non-variadic; the CODE PATH is the same shared marshaling the x86-64 proves with its 9-arg golden — and, honestly: the spill path was NEVER exercised on cross under qemu.
  **UPDATE 21/09:** the decision items above are resolved — variadics = `D-R3-3.5` (option A: **no general variadics**, documented gap R6/R7); opaque handles = `D-R3-3.3` (option A: nominal `Handle` + `Buffer(U8,INOUT)`); D6 struct/array ✅ decided 20/09 with **3.8b JVM landed** (`FfiStructE2ETest` 10/10, `FfiArrayE2ETest` 5/5) and the **D6-3 out-buffer `Buffer(U8)` INOUT landed on the JVM** (`buffer.alloc`/`Buffer.bytes()`; `BufferE2ETest` 4/4, `BufferFfiE2ETest` 4/4). Genuinely still open: Native callback/upcall, Native struct/array/out-buffer + sret, JS struct bridge, `Handle` lifetime.
- **Related:** §61 (CLOSED by this entry — the escape route is now the production route), #431, DB001 (link-by-use precedent), §350 (decl-line diagnostic convention), §342 (translator fa-alias normalization this fix relies on), M32.3 (x86 exit_group rationale the aarch64 missed), `docs/backend-parity.md` FFI rows + `training/idioms/interop.md` (updated in the same commit).

## §370 — `extern` FLOAT slot sem cast explícito vira bit-garbage silencioso no Native (o gêmeo extern do §368; família #431/§369) — ✅ FIXED 20/09 (lowering do call-site converte ao slot; medido no tip `57a0d5f0`+fix)

- **Status:** ✅ FIXED 20/09 (aberto 20/09 pela lane docs, roteado ao cluster #431; fechado pela frente FFI pós-#431 (`DOING.md`), #549 fechável com esta prova
- **Symptom (medido no tip `30412d72`+`d946e6fa`, jar `mvn clean package` + md5 jar==modulo pela regra `docs/debugging/debugging.md` §6):** fixture `float fmid(float a, float b) { return (a+b)/2.0f; }` + `extern "<abs>/libkoffixture.so" fmid(Float a, Float b): Float`:
  - `println(fmid(1.0, 2.0))` (literal Double): **Native imprime `0.0`** (bits double lidos no slot float); **JVM lanca em execucao** `RuntimeException: kof_ffi ... Cannot cast java.lang.Double to java.lang.Float`.
  - `println(fmid(1, 2))` (literal Int): **Native imprime `3.0E-45`** (o inteiro 3 reinterpretado como float denormal); **JVM imprime `1.5`** (correto). Mesmo fonte, mesma lib, saida divergente nos dois formatos — quebra da regra 5 do freeze (paridade cross-target) e do R6 no Native (valor errado sem diagnostico).
  - Os dois programas passam `check` e `build` com **zero diagnosticos** — o gate ausente esta no CALL-SITE dos argumentos de extern declarado, exatamente a doenca que o §368 curou no store de campo.
- **Contrato que FUNCIONA (testado pelo dono, nao disputado):** cast explicito `fmid(4.0 as Float, 9.0 as Float)` → `13.0` byte-a-byte em JVM e Native (`FfiNativeE2ETest` caso "fp", 16/16 re-rodado verde pela lane docs).
- **Root pointer (no edit — lane do cluster #431):** o caminho de argumentos do `extern` (gate `isExternBound` do `BuiltinCallTyper` + marshaling SysV do `NativeFfiCall` + `KofRuntime.kof_ffi`) valida o TIPO da SLOT na linha de declaracao mas nunca roda `TypeChecker.isAssignable` (nem insere a conversao) nos argumentos do call-site como local (`StatementAnalyzer :150-155`), var-decl (`:245`) e — desde `5cd078c1` — o store de campo fazem. Forma do fix pertence ao cluster: rejeitar com diagnostico nomeando a slot (estilo §368) ou converter explicito no marshaling (cvtss2sd/movss), mas Double/Int literal nunca deve chegar ao linker em silencio no slot `Float`.
- **Repro (minimo, 1 arquivo/dir):** `cc -shared -fPIC -o libkoffixture.so fx.c` com `float fmid(float a,float b){return (a+b)/2.0f;}` + `extern "<ABS>/libkoffixture.so" fmid(Float a, Float b): Float` + `main() { println(fmid(1, 2)) }` → `kof build --target native` liga e roda imprimindo `3.0E-45`.
- **Root cause (measured, corrects the pointer above):** the call-site gate DID exist (`BuiltinCallTyper` runs `TypeChecker.isAssignable` per extern argument since #431 slice 1 — `String`/`Bool`/narrowing are `SEM014`), and the KOF contract accepts `Int→Float`, `Long→Float`, `Double→Float` (`isAssignable`: "o lowering emite D2F") and every widening. What was missing was the CONVERSION in the lowering: `ExpressionMethodCallLowerer` pushed the argument raw (Native) / boxed it by its own type (JVM `kof_ffi`), so the SysV marshaling read the bits by the SLOT class and the JVM cast `Double`→`Float`. Same class, not in the original matrix: `sqrt(9)` in a `Double` slot printed `6.67E-162` and `pow(2, 10)` printed `1.0` on Native.
- **Fix (landed 20/09):** new `ExternArgumentCoercion.coerce` (called by both extern paths of `ExpressionMethodCallLowerer`) applies the SAME primitive conversion as an ordinary call (`CompilerEmission2.emitArgumentsWithFormalTypes` → `emitWideningIfNeeded`: I2F/L2F/D2F/I2D/L2D/F2D/I2L) to the declared slot type BEFORE marshaling/box; the JVM path boxes by the slot type. No backend change (`NativeFfiCall` untouched): the backends receive a value of the slot's type, as the calling convention assumes.
- **Proof (measured, WSL Ubuntu-24.04 + JDK 25 + qemu):** RED at tip `57a0d5f0` — `FfiExternTypeConversionTest` 5 of 11 failing (Native `3.0E-45`/`6.67E-162`/`1.0`, JVM `Cannot cast java.lang.Double to java.lang.Float`); GREEN after the fix — **11/11 on JVM, Native and JS host** (`fmaxf`/`ldexpf`/`sqrt`/`pow`/`labs` from real libm/libc, literals AND variables of Int/Long/Float/Double, second-call idempotency, `SEM014` for String/Bool/`Double→Int` and `SEM013` for arity on the 3 targets). The 10-class FFI battery (`FfiSignature`, `FfiE2E`, `JvmFfiCallback`×2, `KofJsFfi`×2, `FfiNative`, `FfiNativeCross` under qemu, `BackendParity`, `DomainGapCodes`) is **94 tests / 0F / 0E / 0 skip BEFORE and AFTER**.
- **Related:** §369 (fatia 1 do #431 — este § e o que ficou do lado do call-site), §368 (mesma classe de gate ausente), #431, freeze regra 5 (paridade) + R6.

## §371 — a CLI SHIPPED nao compila NADA em cross (riscv64/aarch64): o loader de slices le o fonte `.java` do runtime relativo ao CWD -> "prune DESABILITADO" -> runtime completo -> `usesDb` -> `-lsqlite3` inexistente no sysroot cross -> COMP001 ate em `hello.kf` — ✅ FIXED 20/09 (lane `.22`; `ShippedCliCrossSmokeTest` 2/2 + `RuntimeSourceLoaderTest` 6/6)

- **Status:** ✅ FIXED 20/09 (issue #550, lane `.22`) — carga classpath-first implementada na raiz: novo `RuntimeSourceLoader.read` le o fonte de ordem PRIMEIRO do CLASSPATH, com os dois fontes empacotados como recursos de build do `kof-compiler` (`pom.xml` `<resources>` copia `NativeRuntime.java` e `nat/NativeRiscvAsm.java` para as MESMAS coordenadas de pacote; o shade do `kof-cli` os mergeia no uber-jar); o caminho relativo ao CWD foi rebaixado a fallback de DEV (segundo na ordem). Mesma face do android-host (`CompilerPipeline` le `/dev/kof/android-host.kf` via `getResourceAsStream`) — nenhum mecanismo novo, o contrato do cluster nat preservado: a ordem continua DERIVADA do fonte de producao, nunca transcrita.
- **Symptom (medido 20/09, jar `d5c849f3` clean+md5, host com qemu+cross binutils):** `kof build A.kf --target native.risc` com `A.kf` = `main() { println("hi") }` -> `riscv64-ld: nao foi possivel localizar -lsqlite3 [COMP001]`; idem `--target native.arm`. MESMO jar, MESMA fonte, cwd=`kof-compiler/` -> binario gerado e o stderr mostra `prune` ativo. x86 (`--target native`) sobrevive por link-by-use estatico (e porque o host tem `libsqlite3.so` de dev — host limpo sem libsqlite3-dev quebraria no caso `extern`).
- **Mechanism:** `RuntimeSlices.readOrderFromSource` (`:399-403`) e `RiscvSlices.readOrderFromSource` (`:362-369`) fazem `Files.readString(Path.of("kof-compiler/src/main/java/.../NativeRiscvAsm.java"))` — caminho RELATIVO ao CWD. Fora da arvore do modulo (ou seja: SEMPRE que executado do jar distribuuido) lanca `IllegalStateException` -> backend cai no log `prune DESABILITADO ... emitindo runtime completo (fallback seguro)`. O runtime completo contem chamadas `kof_db_*` -> `NativeBackend:259` marca `usesDb=true` -> `:280` forca link DINAMICO -> `-lsqlite3`, que NAO existe no sysroot cross (o proprio comentario de `NativeCrossLink` admete: "CI installs only libc6-*-cross"). As 61 classes `Native*Asm` ja estao no jar; o arquivo so e necessario para a ORDEM das pecas.
- **Blind spot (por que o suite nao pegou):** todos os E2E cross (`NativeRiscv64/Aarch64E2ETest` 42/42, `FfiNativeCrossE2ETest` 6/6) rodam via surefire com cwd=modulo — onde o caminho relativo acha o fonte e o prune liga. O unico artefato que expoe o bug e a distribuicao real (`kof-cli` jar fora da arvore), que a suite nao executa em cross.
- **Proof (medido 20/09, uber-jar `mvn -o -q clean package -DskipTests`, CWD estrangeiro `/home/mel/med/g/hello` contendo SO `hello.kf` = `main() { println("hi") }`):** `java -jar kof-cli-0.4.7-beta.jar build hello.kf --target native.risc --output r64` -> RC **0**, stderr `riscv64 runtime prune 12/60 pieces kept (295759 bytes pruned)` + link dinamico SÓ libc (nada de `-lsqlite3`); `--target native.arm` -> RC **0**, `aarch64 runtime prune 12/60`; binarios ELF reais (`file`: UCB RISC-V / ARM aarch64) e RODAM sob qemu: `qemu-riscv64-static r64/Default/Main` -> `hi` RC 0; `qemu-aarch64-static arm/Default/Main` -> `hi` RC 0.
- **Proof (regressao, mesmo commit):** `ShippedCliCrossSmokeTest` (kof-cli) **2/2** — lanca o CLI como subprocesso de um `@TempDir` FORA da arvore (o cenario do jar shipped via classpath do fork, precedente `CmdBuildFatTest.startCli`) e afirma rc=0 + ausencia de `DESABILITADO` + `runtime prune` ativo + saida `hi` sob qemu nas duas archs; **RED pre-fix com o sintoma exato do ledger** (medido com o fix em `git stash`: `prune DESABILITADO ... libsqlite3.so is not in the sysroot`). `RuntimeSourceLoaderTest` (kof-compiler) **6/6** — os dois recursos empacotados no classpath; leitura classpath-first com caminho de arquivo INEXISTENTE; fallback dev (arquivo) preservado; ausente dos dois -> `IllegalStateException` nomeando as duas fontes (R6); derivação ponta-a-ponta (x86 >=100 fatias, riscv >=40 pecas). Vizinhos (Q4): `NativeRuntimeSliceRegistryTest` 7/7, `NativeRiscvRuntimeSliceRegistryTest` 8/8, `NativeCrossDynamicLinkTest` 9/9 (2 skips honestos de ferramenta).
- **Related:** §369/#431 (fatias 1-2 — o link dinamico sob demanda expos o fallback), `NativeCrossLink` (politica de sysroot), freeze regra 5 (o alvo cross "existe" nos testes mas nao na distribuicao), Q5 (falso-verde por cwd).
